**Chapter Two - The Ever Waking Graveyard**

 *Previously, in the Greysteel Chronicles…*

Smoke filled the air of Stormwind the morning after the attack. The court house in shambles, smoke still rising after the explosions that racked the city the night before. The morning was too quiet. People went about their daily chores and spoke in whispers about what had happened. Many had died that night in the fire.

Stormwind Guards patrolled the city in squads. The captain of the guard leading his men down the canals toward the Pig and Whistle in Old Town. Tripp Blackmoore and his Company were already getting ready to make their exit. He had remained behind, making sure his members were each able to make their way out of the now hostile city. The man waited long enough though, he knew that if he lingered any longer he would be arrested and sent to the gallows quick.

Blackmoore payed several children to help him out. He with his wagon made his way nonchalantly through the canals, straight into the captains patrol. After some heated threats, Blackmoore gave the signal, and the children of Stormwind let out minor explosives from the rooftops, distracting the guards and allowing Blackmoore his escape.

It was apparent they needed to hide, and luckily one of the Greysteel's knew of an abandoned town they could lay low in. One by one they trickled into Raven Hill, and with the help of Blackmoore, they were able to clean it up and make it their own. With a lot of maintenance and TLC - they even managed to thicken the walls and board the windows up just enough to mute the ever present sound of moaning coming from the haunted graveyard in their back yard.

Tensions were high amidst the members of the Greysteel Company. Trust toward their guild leader was very thin, as the company's reputation was in shambles. They were all branded as criminals - traitors to the city. Wanted posters with Ashlynn and Blackmoore's faces were quickly posted, along with the promise of a reward for any known associates. They could not return to Stormwind anytime soon. They needed to find a way to clear their names and pay off their own bounties.

One elf named Barros came to the company with a contract and an offer of his own. The Scythe of Elune was rumored to be within Duskwood. A powerful artifact that was known for the blight that fell upon the woods. If they were to retrieve the artifact and return it to the Cenarion Circle, then Barros would be able to work with the druids to reward the company and possibly remove said bounty. Only if they would prove themselves.

Many members of the Greysteels left within the following weeks. The fear of arrest along with an impossible task was too much of a risk. Many doubted Blackmoore's decision to go after the Scythe of Elune, however the man insisted that it was the only way. If they retrieved that Scythe, then the fame alone for recovering a lost artifact would be enough to clear their names, surely.

As Blackmoore sent scouts out to the surrounding areas to gather as much information as could be found as to the whereabouts of the Scythe, a few of the members decided that it would be within their own interest to strike a deal with those of the Night Watch - after a large construct of flesh and bone attacked them outside the tavern. Darkshire would help by selling them supplies and sending reinforcements when asked.In return the Greysteels would keep the graveyard tame, freeing Darkshire's men to work more in other areas that were quickly falling out of control. The road running through the gloomy forest was a treacherous one. Wolves, Worgen, bandits, all were known to ambush travelers to and from Darkshire. The Greysteels had made their home in a very dangerous place.

Despite the numbers thinning, Blackmoore was determined to continue on this quest to find the Scythe. His scouts had returned with some information regarding the very graveyard that loomed behind their hideout. Still, he addressed those of his Company. He offered them the choice. A resident Warlock had offered a different path, one that would take them north, and to forget the Scythe business completely. A vote was had, and in the end, they decided to continue working with Barros to acquire the Scythe.

A party was made, armor and weapons delivered by Thordin Hammerwill, the company Blacksmith. They ventured into the undead stricken cemetery. Grave Stones older than those left by the victims of wars, a series of elvish runes lead them down into an old crumbling crypt. Other than the ghouls that guarded it, it seemed that no one living had entered these catacombs in a very long time. Bleached bones were scattered along the ground they walked. Elongated skulls hinted that more elves had been laid to rest in these forgotten tombs. Their search eventually sent them through a rather fresh looking dirt tunnel, which lead out into a lab of some sort. Again, guarded by the dead, the Greysteels were forced to defend themselves. Blackmoore lead his men forward, coming across a reanimated thrall they were forced to cut down. Upon it's person, was a note eluding to a place in Silverpine Forest - far North from where they were currently located.

While the Greysteels recovered from their adventure into the crypts, Blackmoore was already working on the next step of his plan. Upon the perfect timing of a letter from a doctor requesting to add his services to the Company, he sent Ashlynn north to meet with the potential recruit as well as to scout out the area to find out where Blackmoore would take the company next. However, Ashlynn probed her nose too far into matters, and got herself captured by a resident in Shadowfang keep, who had heard of their little quest to find the Scythe.

Using a gnomish engineered communication device, Ashlynn was forced into luring the company out to Silverpine. Once they arrived, the Company was forced to split it's forces. Caleth went ahead, cloaking himself in shadows to get a better look. Talvik and Blackmoore lead a squad down into the village below the keep. John, Dolokov, Asta, and Barros bravely chose to brave the keep itself.

The group that went into the town searched far and wide for any clue as to where the Scythe may be hidden. The villagers of Pyrewood were not pleased to have their company. Not long after, the villagers curse reared it's ugly head and they found themselves surrounded by Worgen. They were forced to fight and flee into the city hall which they barricaded until they realized that there was no way out. The idea came to them that they would have trap the Worgen inside and bring down the roof of the building. Their antics nearly killed Thordin. Still, they managed to fight their way out. Upon hearing through the gnomish communication device that this was all a set up, they started fighting their way up to the keep to support the others who had gone inside.

Inside the Keep it was not much more pleasant. Bats, worgen, and undead littered the halls of the keep, ambushing them at every turn. They were given little time to rest, for each time they thought they had a moment to catch their breath, more groups of undead and worgen would come around the corner and charge. John did his best using the light to keep the others going, as Barros lead the way. They were guided by their enemy, wave after wave, deep into the Keep. Upon entering the sanctum, they discovered Ashlynn. Captured and imprisoned by the sorcerer of the keep. It was then they realized it was all a rouse. The Scythe was never here. The intent was to kill the Greysteels and prevent them from going any farther in their search.

With their combined efforts, they managed to defeat the sorcerer and his beasts. Thoroughly ensuring him dead. They rescued Ashlynn and began to make their way back. The body of the sorcerer bursting into blue flames and disappearing as they made their escape.

The two groups met up once again, the first managing to scare the last standing beasts away once they realized their allies had all been slain. After taking some time to mend to the injured, they began their long journey back to Raven Hill. They thought that they would finally be able to take some time to recuperate before the next plan of attack in terms of finding the Scythe. Instead, they were greeted by a horrific sight.

Not only had the tavern been completely ransacked, even worse a mess than it was before, the new furniture tossed over, books and papers scattered, their innkeeper, Mister Finster, cowering behind the counter... In the middle of it all stood one of them. An undead. A grotesque creature in robes with rotting flesh, abscesses, and a single bulging eye, standing in the middle of the carnage, and now before several drawn weapons of the Greysteels, ready to slay him where he stood.

Ashlynn was the one who stopped them, explaining that he was one of them, a member of the company. Much like the orc that had been hired previously. Many were surprised by this, and confronted Blackmoore who informed them that he would hire anyone, no matter what they are or who they were. Stress and tensions were high, accusations were made left and right - threats of leaving the company surfaced. The arguments were interrupted by the screech of what could only be the Dark Riders. Despite being exhausted, several rushed outside, to see the wraiths ride off on their skeletal horses - with what could only be the Scythe of Elune in their possession. Quickly they chased after them, only to lose track of them by the time they hit Deadwind pass.

It was concluded that they only could have gone to Karazhan. A mansion known to be the layer of Medivh. A cursed place of warped magic and free chaos. They needed to prepare for the journey ahead. Entering Karazhan would be no simple task. They needed more money for better armor and supplies. How would they get the money, when they were a band of wanted criminals? It was Ashlynn who came up with the solution, they would host a tournament - in the old abandoned arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Rheya, Caleth, and the undead, Harvey, were tasked to spread posters far and wide across Azeroth to spread the word. Bets were made and collected. The tournament was a success, even the threat of bounty hunters wasn't a problem. It was a much needed break from the realities of life. A chance to get out pent frustrations. To settle old rivalries and start fresh ones anew. Not only did the company profit nicely, but their name seemed to be just a little bit clearer in some eyes. It was a step in the right direction. They even considered perhaps doing a tournament again in the future, learning from their mistakes from this first time - and host an even better one.

At last. They were ready. They knew where the Scythe was. They knew where they must go and what they must do. Blackmoore rallied his company with a speech. This was the day that they cleared their names. That they show the world what the Greysteel Company could do! Despite the fact that Ashlynn had been gone for several days, and did not show to accompany them, they set out. Some with hope, some with their own doubts. As one, they made their way to Darkshire and into the canyon of Deadwind. The wind was harsh in this land, stripping trees bear of branches and leaves. Starving vultures roamed the sky, diving on and assaulting the group, desperate for fresh meat. They fought them off, one by one, as they made their way further down. When they came upon an ogre camp, doubts began to truly set in. The warlock, Terrance, shouted for them to turn back. The group seemed torn to follow Terrance back the way they came, or to continue forward. It was Talvik who put his foot down and convinced them to continue forward. The ogres went down slowly, taking the combined efforts of everyone to bring them each down. Terrance fled while the others pressed on, only to be lifted into the air and brought back to the group forcibly. Outraged, Terrance assaulted Blackmoore, shouting about the futility of this plan and that they should all turn back while they still could.

Then the residents of Karazhan began to appear. The image of a dark rider rushing past the group, an invisible force pushing them aside off the roads. Forward, closer to the mansion itself. They came across a spirit from the past, warning them of the dangers that awaited them and for them to turn back. At first immune to their attacks, she kept pushing them back away from her ethereal form. At their insistence, she promised them their doom and allowed them to pass by, only to begin to slowly stalk after them, other ghosts of the past assaulting them, guiding them toward the crypts laying behind the mansion itself.

At the screech of Darkriders in the distance, they all hurried into the crypts. Blackmoore confronted Terrance about his own accusations, and began to fight the Warlock while the others tried to intervene and begged them to stop. In a rage, Terrance brought forth his own magic, and teleported away, abandoning his allies to the mercy of the dead.

The group made their way into the next room, looking for clues to where the Artifact may be. They opened doors, only to be assaulted by the undead who were disturbed from their rest. Powerful creatures, with more strength then those that wandered aimlessly in the Graveyard back in Raven Hill. It took the strength of everyone combined to cut them down.

The spirit that confronted them outside earlier, appeared once more, and began shouting for her Masters to come for them. Blackmoore and the undead doctor, Harvey, stood their ground as the rest of the group fled, keeping the spirit's attention as the others got away safely. Blackmoore swung at the ghost, but it did little good. At the urging of the others, they made their retreat. Looking back to see that the woman was slowly following along behind them, following them as the company fled down further into the dark crypts. Bodies of the dead were littered everywhere. Some rose from the ground as they passed, forcing them to stop and cut them down before they could continue.

They came to place with water. Dark and murky, with the faintest outline of chains in the distance. A few went through the inky water first, to see if they could find an exit. Upon returning and telling the others, they all made their way into the water, swimming down, passing bloated bodies hanging upside down from the chains. Bits of skin breaking off from the bodies as they disturbed the still stagnate water swimming past them. Upon resurfacing on a lower level of the crypts, they were face to face with the spirit once again, who cackled maniacally at the hopelessness of the company's situation.

Having had enough, those who could weild the light began casting it down upon the spirit. This caught her off guard and she began fending for herself, stumbling backwards, dumbfounded at the impossibility that their magic could reach her. She fought back with her own magic of darkness, scattering it throughout the group. She focused on Blackmoore, taking control of his mind and forcing him to attack his allies. The light was weakening her, however. She vanished on the spot, fleeing from their continuous use of the light against her.

Having thought they defeated the woman, the company continued forward, some moving ahead as other recovered from the fight. A priest named Walt wandered a little too far, examining the massive pile of bones that sat in the corner of an otherwise empty room. The spirit appeared once again, behind the priest and lifted him into the air with a laugh. Others ran to Walt's rescue. Once again lashing out with the light. Thordin threw his light infused hammer straight at the ghost's form. It struck true - cutting a hole right through her ethereal form and passing through into the pile of bones. Her form shimmered and flickered - weakened from the strike - though it was not enough to save Walt. She vanished, along with the priest, leaving the rest of the company one more man short.

Moral at an all time low, the Greysteels had no choice but to keep searching for what they were after. A quick run through the remaining rooms bared no fruit. They returned to the water, and once again subjected themselves to the bloated hanging corpses, swimming to the other side of the pool.

There, among a trove of many other items that had to be magic in nature - there it was. The Scythe of Elune. The relic they had been searching for and sacrificed so much for all this time. The spirit was there before it, waiting for them. Though her form was broken. No longer was she humanoid, but a shade of darkness instead. She did not attack them, nor react to the stream of light magic they were casting upon her. The bright fire in her eyes watched them with interest. She moved aside, allowing them forward into the room, and encouraging them to take their prize. Immediately the company was suspicious. As the druid Barros stepped up to the Scythe, out from the collection rose the dead, dozens of them coming after the group over and over again. The shade's hands began to channel darkness, and the room shook. Rubble from the ceiling began to collapse down onto the Greysteels. The undead continued their assault as the shade channeled her dark magics into the room around them, cackling in a warped, dark, corrupted voice the entire time.

There was no time. Barros lunged for the scythe, but right as he grabbed it a boulder landed right onto it and snapped it in two - leaving him with just a piece. One by one they began dodging the falling rubble, fleeing from the undead. Thordin remained behind to catch the attention of the undead, giving the others a chance to escape. By the time the last one, Asta, made it out, the entrance to the pool of water collapsed - leaving Thordin trapped on the other side with the shade and the army of undead.

Now was the time to flee, they made their way back through the crypts. Keeping an eye out for the dark riders that they knew were near by. They were in no condition for another fight. One by one they managed to trickle out of the crypts and back to the surface. Defeated and broken, the began to make their way back home to Raven Hill. Two men men were lost, and one ran when he was most needed. On top of it all - the very thing they came for, they only managed to grab a piece. Nothing more. Their hopes of turning in the Scythe and clearing their names fading more and more with each heavy step back home.

Barros made his way back to Moonglade to discuss with the druids what they were able to achieve and what further could be done. The rest either returned to Raven Hill or wherever they had made home, to nurse their wounds, drown their sorrow, and await their fate.

Plans for a funeral for Thordin and Walt were discussed. The night ends in silence.

 *To be continued...*

John did his best using the light to keep the others going, as Barros lead the way. They were guided by their enemy, wave after wave, deep into the Keep. Upon entering the sanctum, they discovered Ashlynn. Captured and imprisoned by the sorcerer of the keep. It was then they realized it was all a rouse. The Scythe was never here. The intent was to kill the Greysteels and prevent them from going any farther in their search.

With their combined efforts, they managed to defeat the sorcerer and his beasts. Thoroughly ensuring him dead. They rescued Ashlynn and began to make their way back. The body of the sorcerer bursting into blue flames and disappearing as they made their escape.

The two groups met up once again, the first managing to scare the last standing beasts away once they realized their allies had all been slain. After taking some time to mend to the injured, they began their long journey back to Raven Hill. They thought that they would finally be able to take some time to recuperate before the next plan of attack in terms of finding the Scythe. Instead, they were greeted by a horrific sight.

Not only had the tavern been completely ransacked, even worse a mess than it was before, the new furniture tossed over, books and papers scattered, their innkeeper, Mister Finster, cowering behind the counter... In the middle of it all stood one of them. An undead. A grotesque creature in robes with rotting flesh, abscesses, and a single bulging eye, standing in the middle of the carnage, and now before several drawn weapons of the Greysteels, ready to slay him where he stood.

Ashlynn was the one who stopped them, explaining that he was one of them, a member of the company. Much like the orc that had been hired previously. Many were surprised by this, and confronted Blackmoore who informed them that he would hire anyone, no matter what they are or who they were. Stress and tensions were high, accusations were made left and right - threats of leaving the company surfaced. The arguments were interrupted by the screech of what could only be the Dark Riders. Despite being exhausted, several rushed outside, to see the wraiths ride off on their skeletal horses - with what could only be the Scythe of Elune in their possession. Quickly they chased after them, only to lose track of them by the time they hit Deadwind pass.

It was concluded that they only could have gone to Karazhan. A mansion known to be the layer of Medivh. A cursed place of warped magic and free chaos. They needed to prepare for the journey ahead. Entering Karazhan would be no simple task. They needed more money for better armor and supplies. How would they get the money, when they were a band of wanted criminals? It was Ashlynn who came up with the solution, they would host a tournament - in the old abandoned arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Rheya, Caleth, and the undead, Harvey, were tasked to spread posters far and wide across Azeroth to spread the word. Bets were made and collected. The tournament was a success, even the threat of bounty hunters wasn't a problem. It was a much needed break from the realities of life. A chance to get out pent frustrations. To settle old rivalries and start fresh ones anew. Not only did the company profit nicely, but their name seemed to be just a little bit clearer in some eyes. It was a step in the right direction. They even considered perhaps doing a tournament again in the future, learning from their mistakes from this first time - and host an even better one.

At last. They were ready. They knew where the Scythe was. They knew where they must go and what they must do. Blackmoore rallied his company with a speech. This was the day that they cleared their names. That they show the world what the Greysteel Company could do! Despite the fact that Ashlynn had been gone for several days, and did not show to accompany them, they set out. Some with hope, some with their own doubts. As one, they made their way to Darkshire and into the canyon of Deadwind. The wind was harsh in this land, stripping trees bear of branches and leaves. Starving vultures roamed the sky, diving on and assaulting the group, desperate for fresh meat. They fought them off, one by one, as they made their way further down. When they came upon an ogre camp, doubts began to truly set in. The warlock, Terrance, shouted for them to turn back. The group seemed torn to follow Terrance back the way they came, or to continue forward. It was Talvik who put his foot down and convinced them to continue forward. The ogres went down slowly, taking the combined efforts of everyone to bring them each down. Terrance fled while the others pressed on, only to be lifted into the air and brought back to the group forcibly. Outraged, Terrance assaulted Blackmoore, shouting about the futility of this plan and that they should all turn back while they still could.

Then the residents of Karazhan began to appear. The image of a dark rider rushing past the group, an invisible force pushing them aside off the roads. Forward, closer to the mansion itself. They came across a spirit from the past, warning them of the dangers that awaited them and for them to turn back. At first immune to their attacks, she kept pushing them back away from her ethereal form. At their insistence, she promised them their doom and allowed them to pass by, only to begin to slowly stalk after them, other ghosts of the past assaulting them, guiding them toward the crypts laying behind the mansion itself.

At the screech of Darkriders in the distance, they all hurried into the crypts. Blackmoore confronted Terrance about his own accusations, and began to fight the Warlock while the others tried to intervene and begged them to stop. In a rage, Terrance brought forth his own magic, and teleported away, abandoning his allies to the mercy of the dead.

The group made their way into the next room, looking for clues to where the Artifact may be. They opened doors, only to be assaulted by the undead who were disturbed from their rest. Powerful creatures, with more strength then those that wandered aimlessly in the Graveyard back in Raven Hill. It took the strength of everyone combined to cut them down.

The spirit that confronted them outside earlier, appeared once more, and began shouting for her Masters to come for them. Blackmoore and the undead doctor, Harvey, stood their ground as the rest of the group fled, keeping the spirit's attention as the others got away safely. Blackmoore swung at the ghost, but it did little good. At the urging of the others, they made their retreat. Looking back to see that the woman was slowly following along behind them, following them as the company fled down further into the dark crypts. Bodies of the dead were littered everywhere. Some rose from the ground as they passed, forcing them to stop and cut them down before they could continue.

They came to place with water. Dark and murky, with the faintest outline of chains in the distance. A few went through the inky water first, to see if they could find an exit. Upon returning and telling the others, they all made their way into the water, swimming down, passing bloated bodies hanging upside down from the chains. Bits of skin breaking off from the bodies as they disturbed the still stagnate water swimming past them. Upon resurfacing on a lower level of the crypts, they were face to face with the spirit once again, who cackled maniacally at the hopelessness of the company's situation.

Having had enough, those who could weild the light began casting it down upon the spirit. This caught her off guard and she began fending for herself, stumbling backwards, dumbfounded at the impossibility that their magic could reach her. She fought back with her own magic of darkness, scattering it throughout the group. She focused on Blackmoore, taking control of his mind and forcing him to attack his allies. The light was weakening her, however. She vanished on the spot, fleeing from their continuous use of the light against her.

Having thought they defeated the woman, the company continued forward, some moving ahead as other recovered from the fight. A priest named Walt wandered a little too far, examining the massive pile of bones that sat in the corner of an otherwise empty room. The spirit appeared once again, behind the priest and lifted him into the air with a laugh. Others ran to Walt's rescue. Once again lashing out with the light. Thordin threw his light infused hammer straight at the ghost's form. It struck true - cutting a hole right through her ethereal form and passing through into the pile of bones. Her form shimmered and flickered - weakened from the strike - though it was not enough to save Walt. She vanished, along with the priest, leaving the rest of the company one more man short.

Moral at an all time low, the Greysteels had no choice but to keep searching for what they were after. A quick run through the remaining rooms bared no fruit. They returned to the water, and once again subjected themselves to the bloated hanging corpses, swimming to the other side of the pool.

There, among a trove of many other items that had to be magic in nature - there it was. The Scythe of Elune. The relic they had been searching for and sacrificed so much for all this time. The spirit was there before it, waiting for them. Though her form was broken. No longer was she humanoid, but a shade of darkness instead. She did not attack them, nor react to the stream of light magic they were casting upon her. The bright fire in her eyes watched them with interest. She moved aside, allowing them forward into the room, and encouraging them to take their prize. Immediately the company was suspicious. As the druid Barros stepped up to the Scythe, out from the collection rose the dead, dozens of them coming after the group over and over again. The shade's hands began to channel darkness, and the room shook. Rubble from the ceiling began to collapse down onto the Greysteels. The undead continued their assault as the shade channeled her dark magics into the room around them, cackling in a warped, dark, corrupted voice the entire time.

There was no time. Barros lunged for the scythe, but right as he grabbed it a boulder landed right onto it and snapped it in two - leaving him with just a piece. One by one they began dodging the falling rubble, fleeing from the undead. Thordin remained behind to catch the attention of the undead, giving the others a chance to escape. By the time the last one, Asta, made it out, the entrance to the pool of water collapsed - leaving Thordin trapped on the other side with the shade and the army of undead.

Now was the time to flee, they made their way back through the crypts. Keeping an eye out for the dark riders that they knew were near by. They were in no condition for another fight. One by one they managed to trickle out of the crypts and back to the surface. Defeated and broken, the began to make their way back home to Raven Hill. Two men men were lost, and one ran when he was most needed. On top of it all - the very thing they came for, they only managed to grab a piece. Nothing more. Their hopes of turning in the Scythe and clearing their names fading more and more with each heavy step back home.

Barros made his way back to Moonglade to discuss with the druids what they were able to achieve and what further could be done. The rest either returned to Raven Hill or wherever they had made home, to nurse their wounds, drown their sorrow, and await their fate.

Plans for a funeral for Thordin and Walt were discussed. The night ends in silence.

To be continued...

author: Rudi2
subject: Anselm Meyer: Journal Entries 1 and 2
content_md:
*Journal Entry 1:*
It is June 2nd, Year 615 in the King's Calendar.
My name is Anselm Ernest Meyer the Second. I hail from the old Kingdom of Stromgarde which has fallen prey to the Syndicate and the ogres which are native to the Highlands. This is my first ever journal which I have had the honor in writing in. Such a skill, writing is. I have not picked up a pen in over thirty years! I've had the opportunity to purchase up this blank tome from a greenskin child which traveled with the Darkmoon Faire. He had tried his damndest to peddle this leather-bound book to me in the Lion's Pride while I was enjoying a tall lager after running a few errands from Westfall. I may not be partial to the greenskins, but they sure are stubborn. I paid the boy a silver and picked up a pen from one of the patrons upstairs to borrow for the night as I retire to my room. They'll be back for the pen in the morning.
Scribbling on this parchment gives me fond memories as a quartermaster serving under the Silver Hand. That is, until I was selected for the front line duty. To be fairly honest, I was too damn old for the job, jabbing shambling zombies and rotten ghouls with a long pointy spear. I certainly have came a long way from grace to get where I am now, drinking my earnings and all. I do not know why I am admitting all of this to a book. Strange.
In any case. Here's to a peaceful night; drunked up enough to experience some ol' fever-esque dreams.

 *Journal Entry 2:*
It is now morning, June 3rd. I have, surprisingly, woken up early despite my state of being last night. It may've been early and I just did not realise. I went downstairs to ask the assistant what time it was when I decided to slumber. Apparently it was nine P.M. How odd. Here it is six. I guess the ripe age of fifty-seven affects the human body, and spirit, in strange ways. One of those ways being a terrible sleeping schedule.
Anyways: I remember my dreams fondly, despite being black-out drunk. It appears I've been having the same nightmare that I am usually blessed with when it comes to drinking.
It starts out originally enough, in my old retinue in the Blasted Lands. Just hours before the Kirin Tor had closed the portal for good. I was filled with **rage** back then. I wanted revenge on the blasted greenskins for what they had done to our brothers in Stormwind, where I coincidentally reside in. We were under strict orders to capture any orcs which fled from the portal. I disobeyed said order and put them to the sword. My blade was coated in the dark black blood which those beasts shed. Next thing I know, in the dream, a big flash of arcane light blinds me the moment I corner an orcish family in a small trench. The patriarch of the family put me to the ground, and ran off. I was found in the trench with a busted nose and bloodshot eye by my unit. I woke up after. I understand that what I did was wrong. The Light can not forgive me for such a sin of this magnitude, but my guilt is my penance to bear for the rest of my life. I have been on this planet for over fifty years and have seen three grand wars, and many other little conflicts which scatter the globe. Such a guilt-trip will not be the death of me as I have put that past behind me. All I can do now is lead my life for the better.

subject: Anselm Meyer: Journal Entry 3 and 4
content_md:
*Journal Entry 3:*
It is now June 5th. My travels have taken me from the Lion's Pride in Stormwind to the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Here I enjoy a tall, bitter, but watered down, beer. The whole building smells of... crab? Or is it fish? Turtle?
While it is brightly lit, the whole bar reeks of smoke and torchlight. Hell, I even saw a rat scurry across the counter not long ago before the barmaid's cat snatched it. I can hear chatter and clamour from a group of people who hail from the mercenary company known as ***"Greysteel"***. While a nice, quiet, polite bunch they certainly are too much for this echoey, large building.
I have been tasked with traveling from Westfall, during my errands there, to travel to Redridge to speak with the mayor to investigate the increasing population of bandits and highwaymen on the roads. But upon leaving the bar for the night, some odd thought popped up in my mind..
 **"Go to church."**
It seems as though my instincts have kicked in and, well, here Iam writing while on my way to the Cathedarl Distriht to attend a sermon and confess my wrongdoings for the day. That's easy. Drank and slept. Hell, to be fair I don't recall showering. Even while writing during the sermon I'm getting weird looks from the women and their daughters. Ironically, the Archbishop was speaking about the term "live and let be" which simply means "live by your own belief in other people, and leave others be. Like me.
Oddly enough, the men and sons did not seem to mind my raggedy clothing and stench. Reminder: wash up before hopping on the tram.
Upon leaving after the sermon, I took a bit of a walk around the district. Nice and quiet, it is. I heard some ruckus going on just to the left of the fountain. It appears to be an orphanage. The nanny responsible for the children barged outside with two little cherubs, one boy and a girl. I can't recall what she said specifically, but it appears that the boy snatched some paint from the trade district and dumped it all over the girl's bed.
I went to investigate, as any old cripple does, still donned in my chainmail and bronze armour. The nanny looked up at me and inquired if I just so happened to be an adventurer or not. To which I agreed I was, and she sent the children inside.
"Well. I am." I said.
"Oh, thank the Light!" She exclaimed, promptly reaching out to me for a hug. But after catching wind of my stench, she promptly retracted. I assured her that I was just about to wash up, after that little awkward spell.
"Randis here has been a little troublemaker at the orphanage for a good year now, and there is no sign of change in the boy. I was wondering if you could take little Randis off of our hands for a while and show him what there is to" She said, hushing to a whisper which I mimicked.
"Why is he here in the first place?"
"He lost his parents to the Scourge some time back in Lordaeron. They were adventurers, just like you. He's only eight."
I went quiet after that. It appears as though the undead have taken away the boy's innocence, home, and family. To some extent, I can relate. I, too, was adopted - four years after losing my beloved mother to highwaymen on our way home from Dalaran for some reagents. She was an apothecary. I was around thirteen or fourteen, I believe. I saw it with my own eyes, how they robbed us of every piece of copper we had. They had no interest in the herbs and vials which my mother required to stock the store. They destroyed everything in the horse-drawn cart we so proudly flashed around to our relatives who were farmers just outside of the city, and burnt everything inside. Then, well. I believe I'm done writing about this subject. All-in-all, I accepted to take the boy for a few days, as promised.
I might have met his parents some time in the past during the war. I just wish I could've done something for the boy's parents during that time. Like if I knew then that they would perish.

 *The lower-half of the page appears to be smeared with ink to some degree, and the parchment feels thick to the touch as if it were exposed to water then left to dry.*

 *Journal Entry 4:*
I'm now on the tram with Randis, here.. After visiting the washhouse for the poor in the Cathedral, then after getting directions from an impolite, even smellier dwarf in the Dwarven District. Who actually seemed to be more nicer to the boy than to me, his elder. This is actually my first time on such a device. It appears to run on gears and momentum. During my tenure in the war, all dwarves had was gunpowder and big, **big** firearms. The tanks used appeared to be a mix of gnomish and dwarven engineering. I may be wrong, but oh well.

I have now landed in Ironforge. Again, my first time in such a large city.
"You know. This isn't my first time in Ironforge. It smells pretty bad, doesn't it?" Randis said.
I got a pretty good chuckle out of that and nodded. "Yeah, it's something special."
"Wait. Why are we in Ironforge anyways? Didn't you say you had business in Redridge?"
"That I do, boy. But Miss Nightingale was looking through your things, helping you pick up and all." I said. We had been walking a good distance to the nearest general store for some warm clothes and provisions to help us get through Dun Morogh. "We're going to Loch Modan to see the dam, like you've wanted. She told me after getting the idea from your little journal."
 **"Wait. We are?"**
"A-yup. I might be able to score a few jobs there, as well. So it's a win-win."
That little boy screeched my ear off with excitement. Talking about all the things he's going to buy to throw off the dam. He seemed more excited to visit the dam than he did with a woman he's known all his life read his private diary.
 **That boy has his priorities all messed up.**
So here we are, in the tavern at Thelsamar after showing Little Randis the Stonewrought Dam. He is asleep in the lower levels of the building while I'm enjoying my beer. In comparison to the lager at the Pig and Whistle and Lion's Pride. Those shorties have the bee's knees going on with lager. I will write again soon.

It's 4 A.M. now, Randis is still out for the count. I'll wake him up at around six or six-thirty.

 **I had another dream.**

This time it was in Lordaeron during my tenure in the Scarlet Crusade, which I had the honour of serving under the Ashbringer's son, Renault in the Monastery. I had the privilege of guarding the entrance to the chapel where he and her holiness, Whitemane, had resided. Those two seemed rather close. But something happened that night I was on watch. His brother, Darion had arrived with his father's sword, the Ashbringer itself. Even from there, I had felt the blade give off a sense of oncoming doom, of dread. Just like the last minutes before you pass away. I froze up, staring at Darion and his group of Argents which stared me down like a pariah.
 **"Send for my brother."**
I **bolted** through the chapel's sacred halls, screaming at the top of my lungs" **"COMMANDER? WHERE'S COMMANDER MOGRAINE!?**
The moment I caught eye of Commander Renault, three guards drew blades at me and pointed them. After some explaining, they dropped their guard and, well. Renault came out with a group of men, including me. Next thing I see, Renault is shouting at Darion, whaling his fists into his own brother. I can not explain in enough detail what happens next. The spirit of those brother's father manifests outside of the blade, which laid on the floor just feet away from me. I felt a cold breeze on my neck with each second my eyes laid on that damn sword. The Ashbringer himself picks up his own blade, and struck his son with it. My superior laid dead at his feet. Alexandros left as quickly as he appeared. The sword dropped to the floor. The second the tip of the sword hit the stone floor, I shot up from my bed for the night, covered in sweat and mucus on my face. Randis had been watching me all night, saying I was stirring too much for him to fall asleep. He had my weapon in his hand, saying it was "for protection" because he said I looked like I was being possessed. I gave a chuckle, and he let his guard down some. I sent for a waitress and ordered the boy some stew to calm his nerves.

He's awake now. I guess another day of adventurin' awaits.

It seems as though my instincts have kicked in and, well, here Iam writing while on my way to the Cathedarl Distriht to attend a sermon and confess my wrongdoings for the day. That's easy. Drank and slept. Hell, to be fair I don't recall showering. Even while writing during the sermon I'm getting weird looks from the women and their daughters. Ironically, the Archbishop was speaking about the term "live and let be" which simply means "live by your own belief in other people, and leave others be. Like me.
Oddly enough, the men and sons did not seem to mind my raggedy clothing and stench. Reminder: wash up before hopping on the tram.
Upon leaving after the sermon, I took a bit of a walk around the district. Nice and quiet, it is. I heard some ruckus going on just to the left of the fountain. It appears to be an orphanage. The nanny responsible for the children barged outside with two little cherubs, one boy and a girl. I can't recall what she said specifically, but it appears that the boy snatched some paint from the trade district and dumped it all over the girl's bed.
I went to investigate, as any old cripple does, still donned in my chainmail and bronze armour. The nanny looked up at me and inquired if I just so happened to be an adventurer or not. To which I agreed I was, and she sent the children inside.
"Well. I am." I said.
"Oh, thank the Light!" She exclaimed, promptly reaching out to me for a hug. But after catching wind of my stench, she promptly retracted. I assured her that I was just about to wash up, after that little awkward spell.
"Randis here has been a little troublemaker at the orphanage for a good year now, and there is no sign of change in the boy. I was wondering if you could take little Randis off of our hands for a while and show him what there is to" She said, hushing to a whisper which I mimicked.
"Why is he here in the first place?"
"He lost his parents to the Scourge some time back in Lordaeron. They were adventurers, just like you. He's only eight."
I went quiet after that. It appears as though the undead have taken away the boy's innocence, home, and family. To some extent, I can relate. I, too, was adopted - four years after losing my beloved mother to highwaymen on our way home from Dalaran for some reagents. She was an apothecary. I was around thirteen or fourteen, I believe. I saw it with my own eyes, how they robbed us of every piece of copper we had. They had no interest in the herbs and vials which my mother required to stock the store. They destroyed everything in the horse-drawn cart we so proudly flashed around to our relatives who were farmers just outside of the city, and burnt everything inside. Then, well. I believe I'm done writing about this subject. All-in-all, I accepted to take the boy for a few days, as promised.
I might have met his parents some time in the past during the war. I just wish I could've done something for the boy's parents during that time. Like if I knew then that they would perish.

The lower-half of the page appears to be smeared with ink to some degree, and the parchment feels thick to the touch as if it were exposed to water then left to dry.

Journal Entry 4:
I'm now on the tram with Randis, here.. After visiting the washhouse for the poor in the Cathedral, then after getting directions from an impolite, even smellier dwarf in the Dwarven District. Who actually seemed to be more nicer to the boy than to me, his elder. This is actually my first time on such a device. It appears to run on gears and momentum. During my tenure in the war, all dwarves had was gunpowder and big, big firearms. The tanks used appeared to be a mix of gnomish and dwarven engineering. I may be wrong, but oh well.

I have now landed in Ironforge. Again, my first time in such a large city.
"You know. This isn't my first time in Ironforge. It smells pretty bad, doesn't it?" Randis said.
I got a pretty good chuckle out of that and nodded. "Yeah, it's something special."
"Wait. Why are we in Ironforge anyways? Didn't you say you had business in Redridge?"
"That I do, boy. But Miss Nightingale was looking through your things, helping you pick up and all." I said. We had been walking a good distance to the nearest general store for some warm clothes and provisions to help us get through Dun Morogh. "We're going to Loch Modan to see the dam, like you've wanted. She told me after getting the idea from your little journal."
"Wait. We are?"
"A-yup. I might be able to score a few jobs there, as well. So it's a win-win."
That little boy screeched my ear off with excitement. Talking about all the things he's going to buy to throw off the dam. He seemed more excited to visit the dam than he did with a woman he's known all his life read his private diary.
That boy has his priorities all messed up.
So here we are, in the tavern at Thelsamar after showing Little Randis the Stonewrought Dam. He is asleep in the lower levels of the building while I'm enjoying my beer. In comparison to the lager at the Pig and Whistle and Lion's Pride. Those shorties have the bee's knees going on with lager. I will write again soon.

It's 4 A.M. now, Randis is still out for the count. I'll wake him up at around six or six-thirty.

I had another dream.

This time it was in Lordaeron during my tenure in the Scarlet Crusade, which I had the honour of serving under the Ashbringer's son, Renault in the Monastery. I had the privilege of guarding the entrance to the chapel where he and her holiness, Whitemane, had resided. Those two seemed rather close. But something happened that night I was on watch. His brother, Darion had arrived with his father's sword, the Ashbringer itself. Even from there, I had felt the blade give off a sense of oncoming doom, of dread. Just like the last minutes before you pass away. I froze up, staring at Darion and his group of Argents which stared me down like a pariah.
"Send for my brother."
I bolted through the chapel's sacred halls, screaming at the top of my lungs" "COMMANDER? WHERE'S COMMANDER MOGRAINE!?
The moment I caught eye of Commander Renault, three guards drew blades at me and pointed them. After some explaining, they dropped their guard and, well. Renault came out with a group of men, including me. Next thing I see, Renault is shouting at Darion, whaling his fists into his own brother. I can not explain in enough detail what happens next. The spirit of those brother's father manifests outside of the blade, which laid on the floor just feet away from me. I felt a cold breeze on my neck with each second my eyes laid on that damn sword. The Ashbringer himself picks up his own blade, and struck his son with it. My superior laid dead at his feet. Alexandros left as quickly as he appeared. The sword dropped to the floor. The second the tip of the sword hit the stone floor, I shot up from my bed for the night, covered in sweat and mucus on my face. Randis had been watching me all night, saying I was stirring too much for him to fall asleep. He had my weapon in his hand, saying it was "for protection" because he said I looked like I was being possessed. I gave a chuckle, and he let his guard down some. I sent for a waitress and ordered the boy some stew to calm his nerves.

He's awake now. I guess another day of adventurin' awaits.

subject: Anselm Meyer: Journal Entries 5
content_md:
*Journal Entry 5: Loch Modan to the Wetlands*
Little Randis has followed me from Loch Modan to the Wetlands, after a long and arduous process of helping those who fall prey to the vermin that inhabit this world. Kobolds, ogres, troggs, the Dragonmaw orcs which I myself have encountered in the pocket of Dun Algaz. Randis stayed behind, until I cleared the area. I haven't sat foot in Menethil Harbour for years, to be quite frank. It still looks the same as it did five years ago, aside from different faces.
My first priority was to get a drink and a warm meal in me, as I have lost the taste for saltless lakes and fish which I have been feasting on these past weeks.

Now that I mention the Wetlands and Menethil Harbour, I believe it is high time that I mention why I became an adventurer; to those reading who may find this on my corpse or in my satchel when I'm blackout drunk.

The Light has been on my side since I came from my deceased mother's womb around fifty years ago. She had passed away from bandits who rai.ded our cart we were dragging from Dalaran to Stromgarde, my home city. My father, who couldn't bear with the grief took his own life and left a letter with a considerable sack of coins. The letter, which I still hold in my hands, cannot be copied onto this journal, as the ink has faded away after fifty years of holding it in my satchel.
I was able to avoid conscription during the First War by signing up with the Knights of the Silver Hand, which I had served under for many years until it's reformation into the Scarlet Crusade. During my tenure, I was promoted to sergeant under the ranks of many, many brave footmen which had no training in the ways of the Light, but made it up in tenacity and courage. I could've trained to be a paladin, but giving up my sword and shield for a warhammer would be sacrilege in it's own right.
After witnessing the collapse of the Dark Portal and the sacking of Stormwind: I stayed with the holy order before merging into what little men still stuck with Alexandros Mograine at the time; then continuing into the Scarlet Crusade as a guardsman in the chapel which Renault and Inquisitor Whitemane resided in. Those were the best years of my life. My time under those orders still remain with me in the very recesses of my soul and in my nightmares.
I fled afterwards, catching a boat from my home city of Stromgarde before it fell to ogres and the Syndicate to Menethil Harbour, then a flight to Ironforge to take the tram to Stormwind. I was not greeted a hero's welcome, as many citizens of Stormwind City were refugees from the Third War. They threw food and trash at me the moment I left the Dwarven District to the Cathedral, shouting at me saying their relatives had been murdered by my brothers. I guess it was the isolation in the Monastery which left me dumbstruck as to why those poor citizens were so grudged towards me. Now that I'm in my later years, I do not blame them.
That is when I decided to do better with my life and those around me. I bought a plain suit of chainmail and leather, and a nice two-handed sword and walked to Goldshire, seeing what little I can do. To think that was weeks ago, and here I am taking care of a little boy on my own while at the same time putting gold in my pocket.

Needless to say, I'm doing good.

author: Rudi2
subject: Anselm Meyer: Journal Entries 6
content_md:
**Journal Entry 6: Wetlands to Dustwallow Marsh; to... Astranaar.**
Apparently before retiring to my room, this High Elf woman gestures me over. I will admit, I had one to many the night after writing this. Her name was Vyrin, or something along those lines. Apparently she said for me to travel to a place called "Ashenvale" in a town called Astranaar to service our allies to the west.

Well. Why not? Ships are free to take to and fro. So Randis and I picked up our things from the tavern after picking up my payment for my chores around the city and the region and took the ship to Kalimdor. Landing in Theramore Isle, we did a bit of sight-seeing. This is my first time in Kalimdor, actually. Apparently I'll be seeing more than just High Elves, Dwarves and such here in the west. Things I've only heard tales of in books and drunk ravings. Cow-men who walk on two legs, the Orcs, Night Elves which are native to this land and not refugees in the Park in Stormwind. Floaty... spirits. Odd. Not to mention roving hordes of nomads which have donkey bodies with chests, arms, and legs of men.
Not to mention the way Night Elf society is turned topside compared to Humans. Apparently women run everything. I have nothing against that - after all, there were plenty of women serving the wars and the effort they did at home... I need to quit talking about those times and live in the now.

I have made my way to Astranaar and reported to this Sentinel which gave me a tour of the village, and I soon asked about town in ways I could help. Afterwards, I retired to the tavern to get a nice cold ale. Speaking of Elves again, what the Hell is an "Elune"? Do these peaceful individuals not know of the Light and it's teachings?

...Apparently they don't serve alcohol, let alone brew or distill anything with a kick. What kind of place am I even living in? Already, I hate the High Elf who thought it was funny to send me here. Whatever. Their juices and fruits are actually not that bad, now that I think of it. They even make this thing called a "kimchi". Odd word.

author: Rudi2
subject: Anselm Meyer: Journal Entries 7
content_md:
**Journal Entry 6: Darkshore**
I've been in this continent nary three days now and not a single drop of alcohol in sight. The elves call this "detox" and have been offering me moon... or berry? One of those two juices throughout my days here. Back home they say if you can lay off of the stuff for a couple of days, you have a fighting chance. Thankfully, tobacco is plenty in between with the male demographic of this region. The beds here in Auberdine are pretty comfortable. I have no idea what they stuff their mattresses with. As far as I could care, it'd be leaves or something weird like that. But I have to admit, the Night Elf culture seems to be sticking to me. That all was ruined, sadly, as I met a fellow fisherman who hailed from Ironforge to do some fishin' here and sell the foreign catches overseas. He offered me what little he had in his flask, before he had to run to the elven capital of Darnassus to refuel, since that's the only highly populated settlement that had a demand for such a luxury.
For once in my life, I actually refused a drink. The expression on the dwarf's face quite literally matched mine the moment the words "no thank you" escaped from my lips. He knew what I was thinking, considering the fact he could smell the scent of whiskey and rye on my facial hair. I think the man's name was Blumble or... Bubble? Something that sounded sea-related.
During those three days, going on day four now upon writing this, I had started to experience a slight fever and an increase of dreams which got my heart racing in my sleep. I remember it vividly. During my brief crossing from Dun Morough to Loch Modan, I received a vision of a tall stone human-like structure holding a large weapon of epic proportions. The titan of a person stared down at me in that brief stretch of road in between tunnels, and it spoke to me.

"You dare pass?"

All I could do was stare up at it, speechless. Sometimes my face tends to refuse to show any emotion, and this was one of the many cases. A good hour passed before I could muster up the courage to say something.

"Yes, I dare pass. I'm on a QUEST!"

The titan's voice boomed and bellowed through the congested mountainside, even echoing through the tunnelway which I had just passed through before encountering the monstrosity. I seem to recall being angry and annoyed at the titan. No idea why.

"You have not fled at the sight of me. I shall grant you passage."

And he did. The man disappeared before my very eyes. The last part of the titan to fade away was the large, wide blade he held in his grip which emitted what I could only call "loud" and holy, blinding to the eye.
I woke just seconds after, stepping into the tunnel which the titan had played gatekeeper to. My bed was soaked in sweat and sputum. After a moment of getting back to my senses, I went downstairs, washed up, and informed the innkeeper to get new sheets.
A few minutes in, the innkeeper came down and went back to their usual business in the early morning. I ordered some of that kimchi they took pride in and just ate alone with my thoughts to keep me company.

I noticed that I did not speak of Randis anywhere in this segment. Well, needless to say Randis got what he wanted. I didn't spend much time talking to the boy, after all I was just told to show him what I do in my life. Kill beasts and bandits, talk to people, get paid and go on my merry way. Needless to say his origin story is what will lead him to become a good adventurer. I sent the boy up to the ship from Auberdine to the village that lets you into Teldrassil, and employed a sentinel to keep an eye on Randis while he took in the sights and sounds of such a foreign land on the way to Darnassus. Then after he saw the tree, he was to see a magnus who could teleport him back to Stormwind. Whole damn venture took almost two gold out of my pocket. One for the portal home and the other for the sentinel.
In retrospective, I do feel kind of bad for kicking the boy out of my life so soon. But it is a means to an end. He will get sided with yet another adventurer - one like me - and do the same old schtick. Can't say I blame the boy for wanting to grow up for the better.

That reminds me, though. I haven't reminded myself of this until now, but what of my life back home? All I used to do was take care of drunks and occasionally beat down kobolds and Defias in Goldshire. (I kept that part out of the past few entries. It just didn't seem to fit right with all the edginess to the entry about my life.) I have a hefty coinpurse, some good equipment and weapons. But it just feels natural. What irks me the most about this new lifestyle is the constant moving around and change of scenery, which is why I look back on my days in Elwynn.

author: Thiccroy
subject: Dolokhov Steelblood's Journal - 1 "The Journey Here"
content_md:
**Twenty-fifth of the Sixth Month, 30 ADP.**

Long have I not written in any parchment that may touch my hands, but the sudden freedom and chance to record what has happened to me this past month is undeniable, to say the least.
Suddenly, my life seemed to turn for the better, an upward spiral of sorts.

It has been one month since the day I set out from Stormwind. My mentor, Grish, a Warrior-Cleric and veteran of the Great Wars, had taught me what I knew. I had only a flimsy shield, sword and basic cloth and leather wear to accompany me and my ninety copper.

Soon enough, I was in Goldshire, helping the Marshal with scouting out Kobold threats. Kobolds, nasty creatures. if you're not careful in dispatching them, I've gathered, they screech and screech and the echo of their endless mines, caves, and tunnels brings forth more of these infestive rat creatures. They are easy to kill, but hard to manage. Through these adventures, I gained more coin, and one night whilst using my coin to gain drinks from Lion's pride I met a boisterous and carousing Dwarven Warrior called Gallegund.

Gallegund became my friend and teacher for a long while. Together, we killed Defias Bandits within the forests of Elwynn and scoured their camps for stacks of loot and sums of money. Soon enough, I was richer than I had ever been these past ten years. It was an adventurous time, and soon enough, I had to leave the confines of the Forest.

The Marshal had given me a mission to go to the Captain Stoutmantle of Westfall, the leader of an inspiring group of warriors and rangers calling themselves the People's Militia. I could not deny my urges to help these people. They seemed to be most akin to my own blood, as their lands were not the most important, but the families and names around them. That was the point of the militia, and the farmers and small folk out for themselves amidst marauding outlaws and vagabonds.

The Defias proved to be too much to handle alone, and I had, for the first time, met a trainee paladin, and an adventuring Kaldorei Druid. The Paladin was Ulf, skilled in two-handed weaponry. He had taught me much of the long blade, and I began to use a sword that I had looted from a Defias camp. The druid was Myrt, an interesting man for an elf. I had long heard the Kaldorei had been a serene and patient people. But this druid, within his 'Bear Form' was a furious and hot-headed force to be reckoned with. he was young, I garnered, and as much as a trainee in his arts as Ulf.

All three of us met with Ghosts by a Lighthouse (Don't ask me), and killed vermin ranging from gnolls, to murlocs, to kobolds and various creatures of the vast plains of Westfall, for a kind lady of a farmhouse to make stew for us. I must say, despite the contents, it was like a gourmet dish.

Together, we improved our skills in Blacksmithing and Mining, and I had improved greatly in First Aid. My arts, skills, money, and armor had improved immensely over the past month, and I felt proud. I did not feel meek anymore...

My journey was headed North, one day. Somehow.

I will come back to you, sweet Strom.
I shall avenge you.

Long have I not written in any parchment that may touch my hands, but the sudden freedom and chance to record what has happened to me this past month is undeniable, to say the least.
Suddenly, my life seemed to turn for the better, an upward spiral of sorts.

It has been one month since the day I set out from Stormwind. My mentor, Grish, a Warrior-Cleric and veteran of the Great Wars, had taught me what I knew. I had only a flimsy shield, sword and basic cloth and leather wear to accompany me and my ninety copper.

Soon enough, I was in Goldshire, helping the Marshal with scouting out Kobold threats. author: Thiccroy
subject: Dolokhov's Journal - 2 - "Blackrock and Roll"
content_md:
**Twenty-seventh of Sixth Month, 30 ADP.**

"I dream of walls,
and hearth of wood.

A home of peace,
Both fair and good.

My love is there,
in Stromgarde's Halls.

Waves of the sea,
on Hills of Old.

And 'ere I went,
to lift my hand.

I left my heart,
upon the sand.

When duty's done,
and glory earned.

I swore my heart,
I would return."

I suppose I should start off with what I had been doing recently. Recently, for my reputable work, I was employed by the Magistrate of Redridge, Lord Solomon for three things. Luckily, I had my friend and trustful ally, Gallegund, with me.

I and Gallegund were tasked with bringing back a lost soldier to Lakeshire, and tracking down and killing two warlords in the Blackrock ranks. Gath'Ilzogg and Taran'zul. Both were monstrous and large, as the descriptions went. They did not do them justice. Choosing to rescue the soldier first, we set out north, through the burnt valleys bordering the Burning Steppes. Along the way, I was interested in how they came to be so.

Gallegund told me histories I really should have learned. His people were once under a mighty High King, three centuries ago, before the King died and the three clans of the Dwarven race split in a three-sided war. Amidst it all, the foolish Dark Irons released a mighty God of Fire, called 'Ragnaros'. So strange. Why would they willingly put themselves to slavery and destroy so much beauty?

Either way, we fought our way through sorcerers of dark magic and demons, and various warriors in lackluster mail and leather. We swiftly found Corporal Keeshan within the depths of a mine. He was hurt, on his last legs, but he saved me from a near decapitation. He had some fight in him. A man who had skill even after losing his comrades and much blood. I must respect the tenacity of these Azerothians.

Handing him to one of the Guards, we took our reward and set our way to our most challenging moment yet. The Castle, Stonewatch, once stood proud during the First War and before. However, the Orcs had razed it, and the Blackrock had not left it since. Within we found Taran'zul in its courtyard. The warriors and sorcerers around him were great and powerful, outfitted and trained better than the rest.

Indeed, it was a hard and bloody fight, with near deaths with both of us. Soon enough, Taran's head was ours, and we dived into the Garrison itself. Its rickety floor, old and burnt in some spots, creaked at each step, and so, the Blackrocks came in like a furious tidal wave when hearing us. Dispatching them with cunning tactics of close quarter combat and hallways, we made our way up to the War Room, where Gath'Ilzogg was waiting.

If it was naught for Gallegund cutting off the beast's arm, we would not have made it out of there. He had a fiery black dragon with him, a whelp. I can still feel his heat on me. Hmph. Either way, the Warlord was dead, his head ours. We quickly escaped as more reinforcements came, and soon found ourselves resting in the Inn.

After that, Gallegund, for rewarding me for 'getting out of that alive', he gave me new armor. He showed me his skills in blacksmithing, forging a mighty blade that did not burn on the inside, but burned your hand when you grasped it too long and spewed forth flame like a dragon at each swing! Marvelous! I must learn more about the art of hammer and anvil. The Dwarves have secrets and arts I -must- explore and know!

Now is night. I hear the patter of soft rain, and the jingle within my coin purse makes me happy. Hope and justice is on my side, and I am getting closer to my goal.

I swore my heart that I would return.

author: Thiccroy
subject: Dolokhov's Journal 3 - "The Greysteels and the Scythe"
content_md:
**Seventh of the seventh month, 30 ADP.**

Light.

Where to begin?

As I rest in the lower bunk of a two bunked bed, above me the very 'heavy' Gallegund, I begin to draw my thought to the events that began a week ago, taking me to Silverpine and back. Making me face Worgen, Ghosts, the Undead, the Shadows of the past, all to find an elven Scythe and avenge the curse of the wild beasts that roamed those forests.

It all began in Darkshire. I was traveling around, collecting contracts that I could finish in these abandoned, dark woods. I made my way to the most western hamlet in the province, the cemetery town of Raven Hill. There, in the inn, I met and spoke with Gallegund, as others began to appear. It seemed to collect quite a crowd, to which I found out that they were the Greysteel Company. And by Gallegund's accounts, wanted by Stormwind.

I kept my calm as we inquired about a possible contract with them. We both found out we were looking for a Scythe that had been used by a powerful sorcerer called Arugal, called the Scythe of Elune, which summoned monstrous beings that I had never heard of before- the Worgen.

Our path would lead us to Silverpine, which I was surprised about. But twelve gold was twelve gold, and I and Gallegund accepted this mission.

Soon enough, as I, Gallegund and the company gathered around Blackmoore, their Captain, we became aware of the capture of one of their spies within Silverpine, who was looking for the Scythe and Arugal. What happened would haunt me forever.

Teleportation.

I head eaten mutton, potatoes and drank it down with good Lakeshire Kvass. However, I had deposited most of it on the cobbles of a road not far from Pyrewood Village. We had teleported into hostile territory and we were all dazed as we continued our path. Our large party split up. As they always do in these kinds of stories...

One larger party traveled into the Village. Within it was Gallegund, to whom I told my goodbyes to as I traveled with a smaller, quicker and stronger party up the steps to Shadowfang Keep, the place of Arugal and his power, and possibly, hopefully, the Scythe. With me was a Kaldorei Druid called Barros, hell-bent on the destruction of Arugal. There was a senile, old priest, called John, who had insulted me and my people before, but we learned to cooperate with one another. Then there was Asta, a Lordaeronian Dame, who wielded shield and light. I, with my large two-handed blade, traveled into its deep halls and battlements with them.

It had been the first time I had seen Worgen. That I had seen ghosts of all things. I had not thought it would be so easy as to kill ghosts. Our first task was to get into the courtyard, forcing us to fight through hounds and bi-pedal hounds. The Worgen were mighty and strong but they proved naught enough for the four of us. John healed and invigorated us, as Barros took the brunt of the damage in his bear form, while I and the Dame took on dispensing justice and flanking attacks at the enemies around us.

The battle was long, but after killing a Worgen Alpha in the stables, we were quick to unlock a Wizard of the Kirin Tor from his cage. Not catching his name before he departed, he had promised and delivered his gratitude by opening the courtyard doors for us. There, we fought Ghosts, who put temporary hexes and spells upon us. On a small detour, the Dame Asta had a quest from a blacksmith to bring her a hammer within the courtyard's stables. She had, foolishly, thought it was... Inside one of the horses.

We killed them. Of course, they were hellish looking, but Barros did not approve. I thought nothing of it. I, Asta, John, and Barros continued up to the upper levels, dispensing justice upon the Worgen through the hallways and battlements. We were getting close to the Commander of the army of Ghostly Guardsmen upon the walls but were soon ambushed from the back by the ghost of the Baron Silverlaine himself, and some of his ghostly goons. The ambush was sudden, but not enough to halt us.

We pressed into the Commander's War Room and soon dispensed with him. I had found it interesting, that the Commander's ghost could 'heal' itself with what seemed to be the light. I shook this off, as the Dame Asta prayed for his lost soul, so he may go on from his eternal curse.

Soon came a battle against an army of ghost guardsmen, which we narrowly fell in, but after a small pause, continued our way into a tower of alchemic research, filled with tomes and libraries. Running up winding stairs, we came upon the biggest hound I had ever seen. It was the height of three Kaldorei Elves, and as we stood by, I manned up and charged in first, followed by Barros and the other two. It was quick to kill, considering its size, but the cage doors behind it could not be opened. It was a trap, as shadowy like beings appeared behind us and attacked us!

We quickly dispensed them and proceeded to the last enemies. A large worgen waited for us up some steps, and we swiftly killed it to proceed through a large gate. There, Arugal stood, with the Lady Ashlynn, tied and beaten. The priest, John, tried to coax him with rude behavior and vulgarity, but it was to no avail. I, Asta and Barros would run in and fight his 'Sons of Arugal', large, alpha Worgen, as John fought his darkness with his Light. Up above, we saw as John, by himself, dispensed with Arugal, a mighty mage, by taking the form of -pure shadow-. Incredible. terrifying.

As the others took care of Ashlynn's wounds, I scoured Arugal's perch for the Scythe.

The Scythe was gone.

We quickly ran from the Keep, as Arugal's disembodied voice laughed at us. He had not been killed, I gather... Or maybe he was. We left the Keep behind, and an angry Blackmoore screamed to the heavens. We had come for naught, almost losing two men, although I would not have been sad about one of those deaths, an Alteraci called Talvik.

So began our week-long journey home. We had walked through Southshore and I had departed to Stromgarde. There, for two days, I had stayed, before meeting the party again in Dwarven lands. Together, we took the Tram to Stormwind and made our way to Raven Hill, to be paid and rest. However, within the inn, we found out the treachery and madness of Blackmoore. The fool had recruited an undead! An undead! I had almost cut off both their heads, but we were distracted by the sudden appearance of these 'Dark Riders', holding the Scythe itself to them.

We tried to catch them, but to no avail, and as I and Gallegund said our goodbyes, we returned here to Darkshire.

I must sleep. And shave.
And count my money.

It is soon time to enact my ambition. My promise. My oath.

I swore I would return.

author: Kazgrim
subject: The Broken Chain
content_md:
In an instance, the blindfold was lifted from Ghrakraz's scarred face. No longer was he filled with such immeasurable rage. He looked around him to find his brothers exhausted and confused, and feeling the same burden lifted from his shoulders. For a moment he forgot who he was, where they stood. But their demon masters became aware that their hold upon the orcs was no longer, and so Xhak'ariz ordered their slaughter.

Now, Ghrakaz felt a new rage stir within his heart. A force born not out of a desire for destruction, but to save his people from doom. He raised his axe, and just as the hero Grom delivered our race, freed our clan from the clutches of the burning shadow.

And that, my child, is the day the chain was broken.

content_md:
**The Greysteel Brawl**

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/579523935498928130/596144268339445800/pngkey.com-sword-png-252822.png)

 *Do you seek honour? How about glory? Mayhaps you seek the greatest of jungle brews that Stranglethorn can offer? Then the Greysteel Brawl is for you! Rules of the Game!

The tournament is going to be in two sections: One is going to be your normal duel using the mechanics of the game and the second one using rolls. For the first tournament to make things fair as much as we can is going to be like this:

The first tournament is going to be hosted by brackets of 4 levels, looking like this:

 **10-14 / 15-19 / 20-24 / 25-29 / 30-34 / 35-39/ 40-44 / 45-49 / 50-54 / 55-60**

The tournament is going to be divide between the melee classes and the range/caster classes so is going to be like this:

Mages, Warlocks, Priests And Hunters (Druids/Shamans)
Warriors, Rogues And Paladins (Druids/Shamans)

The hybrid classes like the druid and the shaman can join only one section of the tournament, for example a druid that decides to participate in the range/caster section can't participate in the melee one.

 **PvP Rules:**

 1.- No consumables (Potions, runes, foods and etc)
 2.- No engineer stuff (Trinkets, grenades, etc)
 **3.- The use of bandages is allowed**
 4.- Can't use buffs that are not from your class (Paladins can only have one blessing, the using of potions for buffing is not allowed)
 **5.- Weapon procs are allowed, for example if you weapon have a chance on hit of casting a frostbolt is valid.**
 6.- Each elimination phase is going to consist of only one round. The final duel is going to be the best of 3 rounds.
 7.- In case that only 2 people show for one bracket, the winner is going to be decide by the best of 5 rounds.

The second tournament is much more simple and is going to be like this:

Each duelist is going to /roll and the one that gets a higher number is going to make one hit, the first one to make 3 hits against their rival is going to win. There is no level require to participate in this tournament. It would be recommended that people use /emote each time they try to take a strike for more immersion.

 **Example of how this will play out.**

 *Ashlynn takes a ready stance, holding her sword with both hands. It looks way too heavy for her. With a grunt, and then a yell, she threw herself at Blackmoore, using all her strength to swing her blade down onto Blackmoore's shoulder.*

Ashlynn rolls 12
Blackmoore rolls 15

 **Blackmore 1 / Ash 0**

 *Blackmoore laughed, knowing that Ashlynn hardly knew how to use a sword at all. He casually side stepped, letting Ashlynn's momentum carry her forward and would turn around to face her. Like the cheeky bugger he is, he attempt's to swat Ashlynn's bottom with the flat side of his sword, a cocky grin on his face.*

Blackmoore rolls 17
Ashlynn 3

 **Blackmoore 2 / Ash 0**

 *Ashlynn let out a gasp as she felt the heavy metal hit her, and she turned around, eyes narrowing and face reddening. With another cry, she held the too-heavy sword above her head and charged at Mister Blackmoore, pulling the sword around in an arc to attempt to cut into the man's side.*

Ashlynn 19
Blackmoore 13

 **Blackmoore 2 / Ash 1**

 ----------------------------------

In order to save time, regarding /roll dueling, it will be one round per combatant - pitting winners against each other until we finally have a winner!

Good luck my fellow turtles.

 *And may the odd's be ever in your favor.*
