subject: War Stories:Odysseus Bunce
content_md:
This is the journal of a Stromic Noble,

Page 1.

I am Odysseus Bunce, noble and mage of Stromgarde, I hail from the House of Bunce. I signed up to the Alliance army together with my three brothers, it has been years since the second war ended and the Orcish Horde was defeated. The Various human kingdoms are at peace and the elves keep to themselves ever ignorant to the politics of their southern comrades. The Orcs in the interment camps are as lifeless as ever, carrying on every day without meaning however there are orcs who refuse to be bound to their fate of slavery and are revolting, freeing others from the interment camps and raiding human villages. Seeking glory and honor for the family my brothers signed up for the Alliance army. Due to their noble heritage and the history of our house they were trained as commanders, to lead the infantry of the armies in combat and to serve under generals. I myself being more of a bookworm from the days I spent in dim light of the candles reading various books on history and magic. Had been studying any magic I could, even having visited Silvermoon in many occasions to talk to the mages of the famous city and perhaps even study under them. I was instructed to accompany the mages of Dalaran that were in our army group to assist and fight alongside them. Our training was done a week ago and we are being sent to put down a uprising in the Arathi Highlands. I wonder what kind of Orcs we'll be fighting.

Page 2.

The Orcs were far more organised than we originaly expected. We were only informed that the orcs were rebelling inside the interment camp and had taken over the camp, but what we instead arrived to was a organised operation, the orcs had help from the outside and were clearly part of a greater operation and band of orcs, they not only took the camp but fortified it, making it into a base for those savages. Upon arrival our forces were ordered to engage a full assault on the camp, but the orcs had weaved foul magics inside the very walls of the camp and our siege engines struggled to break them. Luckily it was no real castle otherwise we would have suffered even greater casaulties than we had. The commander of the dalaran portion of the army, to which I was assigned suggested that the mages of our army could weave a spell that would not only break the spell upon the walls but also breach them. With that being decided as our course of action we were lucky to succeed, but the orcs nonetheless continued their resistance. We took the Camp and took no prisoners, the orcs had tasted freedom and paid their price. And we paid a heavy price in the form of sacrifice of our soldiers who died in the assault for the continuation of peace. For now we are to be stationed in the camp, but talk amongst the commanders is that we'll be sent north to Lordaeron, who knows, I hope I'll see Capital City, uncreative name really.

Page 3.

It's good that they supply soldiers and the like with anything they require... but we are running low on certain supplies. I just hope that we resupply quickly. On other news we are moving rather quickly through Silverpine Forest. We just passed Shadowfang Keep today, I remember visiting it as a kid, Father always did make sure to take all of his sons with him on important trips. Otherwise nothing really is going on that is interesting. We passed the town of Soutshore with no problem and some men visited Tarren Mill to spend some time with their families. We're part of a diverse army made up of Dwarves from Dun Morogh, Humands from Stromgarde and Lordaeron, shame that the men from Gilneas were recalled due to the policies of King Greymane, they were good people so I guess it's best for them to leave. Most of the mages are from Dalaran ofcourse, but for some reason a few mages from Silvermoon have joined our ranks. A lot of the men are made nervous by this but the commander says that it's just the High Elves doing their minimum effort. who knows? We can see Capital City in the distance, and some say that Prince Arthas and Uther the Lightbringer dealt with an orc raid. Hopefully the Orcs will be put a stop to soon. I wonder if We'll meet them on the way to our next post.

Page 4.

We reached the town outside of Capital City today, but strange news come from the nearby towns. People that fled to Brill (The town we are currently stationed at) are saying that the end of Azeroth has come, that people started getting sick in their villages after the grain shipments came in. And soon after that people started dying, more disturbingly they report that the people that died after getting sick somehow got back up and started attacking people. Whether or not these claims are true or not I think will be revealed soon. We had a meeting about this(I was suprised I was invited but I suspect my brothers were responsible for this.) and my brother Amaran was sent to investigate the nearby villages with a small detachment of our forces to put our mens hearts to rest. The sun will soon set and we are to move out soon, I'll end this page here.

Page 5.

It was madness! I was awoken during the night in my chambers by a loud knock on the door. One of the captains was sent to wake the mages and he informed me that peasants were dying left and right. The dead were rising and attacking the town, I quickly gathered my things and sallied out with the other mages. I couldn't believe it the undead were attacking from within the town, the villagers and soldiers who died rose up again to fight us. With fire and frost we tried to hold the undead back. Luckily we survived the night but lost quite a few men. We're forced to recruit from the locals who did survive the night to replenish our forces. The rumors were true and it turns out that some of the Dalaran mages were somewhat informed about the odd shipments. We'll be forced to stay in Brill for a while more and the men are working on fortifying it in case more of the undead attack. There has been no news or messengers from by brothers Amaran's forces. And I hope that he's alright, afterall the claims of the peasants were proven to be true. One of my brothers argued for immediatly setting out to look for Amaran but he was denied, we would have rode for his forces if only there was not the threat of desertion. We'll be sleeping with weary and worried hearts tonight.

Page 6.

To our suprise many of the men from the town, and even many more refugees joined our forces. The day was spent training them and equiping them, the smithies were working day and night for our forces to have enough weapons and armor. The scouts had reported a large mob of the undead nearby one of the villages but they were not able to see if the force was of former soldiers or just a mob of undead peasants. Although I hope it's not Amaran's detachment there is a very high possibility that it's his force. We'll be setting out for it soon. We haven't got any orders from the General and the news from the Kingdom of Lordaeron that we are currently stationed in are not boding well. The grain is plagued and our supplies are being heavily rationed. The other mages say that the source is magical, maybe we can find a cure to this illness? Whatever it is that is raising the undead it reminds me of the stories of how the orcs used the undead to wage their war against the Alliance. Orc Necrolytes they were called.

Page 7.

My suspicions were correct, we encountered the undead force that was made out of my brothers Amaran's forces and whatever undead gathered to them. I hoped that he had survived and escaped but no, We engaged the undead on a flat terrain and their numbers seemed endless. the men that were slain rose again to bolster their numbers and we were fighting a losing battle. many undead fell to flame and the arcane with many mages conjuring elementals to bolster our forces since they could not turn those against us once they were slain. In the end we saw my brother now an undead commander leading the forces, we were forced to retreat. We heard of Prince Arthas' forces in the east marching for Stratholme. Hoping to join up with them and perhaps ending this madness and scourge that has befallen the North. Perhaps the paladins will prove a powerful weapon in this fight.

Page 8.

We could not believe our eyes when we arrived in Stratholme, the city was set ablaze and those we encountered said that the crown prince of Lordaeron grew mad and set aflame to the city in paranoia. Our commander met with the Sorceress Jaina Proudmoore, daughter of the Kul Tiran king and apprentice to Andromath. We will be sailing west for some reason. I don't know what kind of madness this is but orders are orders. The undead hordes of Lordaeron are growing larger and we wont be able to handle them much longer. Arthas has gone North in his mad quest to slay some sort of "Dreadlord". We'll be heading to a port near Capital city to sail past Maelstrom. Some men thought about deserting our forces but were quickly reminded of what awaited them in the wilds of Lordaeron. I hope alls well in Stromgarde.

Page 9.

We set sail for a land to the west, there's so many citizens.... Hoping to escape the hellfire that they left and I can't blame them for being so hasty to abandon their homeland.  Even now news are spreading that the demons have returned to Azeroth to set it ablaze. We have enough supplies to last the massive fleet for a few month. It's a wonder that we were able to gather so much. The land that we leave behind may be the last that we ever do. We know that this is a risk, but we made our choice. I just hope Lady Proudmoore is right and there is a continent to the west which is on no known map. We're counting on finding it soon to keep up the morale.

Page 10.

Landfall! We have made it to what the men are starting to call Kalimdor. But the land is a harsh one, we landed in a Desert which showed few signs of plantlife. We were ordered to move west in a mountainous area to build a fortress and seek out a Oracle. I myself would not trust any peddler of magic, much less in a strange land that has been just discovered. Scouts report that orcs were spotted in the nearby desert that we landed in, having sailed here with human ships. Perhaps they followed us? No matter, if they come for us we'll be able to cast the green savages back into the tides!.

Page 11.

The Orcish Horde, lead by a invidual called Thrall (Calling their Warchief a slave? These Orcs are strange) attacked us. Their forces burned down the fortress to the ground and we were forced to flee into the caverns, many suprises were found in these caverns but in the end we made an uneasy alliance with the Orcs.... I do not know what madness has befallen upon them but the Orcs seem to have the same goal as us. We're being sent North to a forested region to set up a base. I dont trust these orcs but I was made commander recently. I was placed in charge of a expedition force made out of Humans and Orcs alike. I hope we can get this over with quickly before the orcs decide to break their promise and betray us. My brothers were sent on similiar missions, my brother Garadol further up north, and the youngest of us Barrdol was sent east.

Page 12.

We were attacked whilst gathering lumber for our fortress, the assailants were similiar to the High Elves of Silvermoon but their skin were of different shades of purple and they seemed to refuse the use of the arcane. We defeated their forces but were later assailed by much worse enemies. The demons had tracked us to this continent and laid siege to our newly built bases. We barely held out and I had sent a missive to the main force for reinforcements. I had also sent news of the Elven natives which had attacked us to Lady Proudmoore although I am sure they already know of them.

Page 13.

I do not know what is going on in her head but Lady Proudmoore has made yet another unreasonable alliance, this time with these "Night Elves". She has called for our forces to assemble on the tallest mountain on Kalimdor called Mount Hyjal to defend some kind of Tree from the Demons. Although I can recognise magical places and their worth it's still insane. If the elves had their way they would have us all die there. I must follow orders though and I am glad I will be able to rejoin my brothers Garadol and Barrdol.

Page 14.

The defense of Mount Hyjal proved costly, my own brother Barrdol was slain when the demons breached our base. But he fought like ten lions, like a true stromic hero he paid with his life so we could buy time for the elves and their plan. Bit by bit we were beaten back suffering ever greater casaulties assaulted by demons and undead alike we were beaten back to the orcish base and even further until we were near the Elves holy tree. The leader of the Demons, Lord Archimonde I believe he was called fell in battle, we had won the battle and our duty was done. We traveled to a land we would eventually call Dustwallow Marsh and established a city called Theramore. It'll be good to rest our bones. and to lay to rest those we have lost, including Barrdol.

Page 15.

It has been months since the legions defeat, we've had to hunt down any remaining demon forces and it seems the uneasy alliance or well, rather truce persists. The orcs were allowed to build their infernal city in the north which they have started to call Orgrimmar. We've established a working relationship with the Night Elves and have even begun trading with them. I've grown to mingle with many of them and although I disagree with many of them, I have grown to respect them. It's quiet and peaceful for now, and we have regained contact with the Human Kingdoms and the rest of the alliance. It's horrible what happened, Arthas has destroyed Lordaeron and Silvermoon, Dalaran has fallen and I don't even know what's happening to Stromgarde. I hope news reach us soon.

Page 16.

I was suprised by who of all people showed up to Theramore of all people, Lord Admiral Daelin Proudemoore himself. A hero of the alliance, he called for all those who wished revenge upon the Horde and with no suprise many joined them. The Orcish menace has to be wiped out one way or another. This is just putting them out of their misery, my brother Garadol agreed to coming with Daelin's forces when I asked him. Were making plans on attacking Durotar, and we have already taken the Echo Isles. We'll be moving on to Orgrimmar soon to finish the job.

Page 17.

The Orcs beat us back, it seems some sort of abomination, a filthy breed of Ogre and Orc lead the Orcish forces, bolstered by ogres trolls and tauren alike to combat against us. My brother Garadol fell to that blasted brutes hand and we couldn't even retrieve his body. This is a lost cause and we have retreated to Theramore. I wont waste my time on Daelins crusade anymore, I'm getting back to Stromgarde one way or another. And after that to Lordaeron, I will find what happened to my brother Amaran and hopefully lay his spirit to rest.

This was written by Odysseus Bunce, last of House Bunce and the son of Strom.

Page 7.

My suspicions were correct, we encountered the undead force that was made out of my brothers Amaran's forces and whatever undead gathered to them. I hoped that he had survived and escaped but no, We engaged the undead on a flat terrain and their numbers seemed endless. the men that were slain rose again to bolster their numbers and we were fighting a losing battle. many undead fell to flame and the arcane with many mages conjuring elementals to bolster our forces since they could not turn those against us once they were slain. In the end we saw my brother now an undead commander leading the forces, we were forced to retreat. We heard of Prince Arthas' forces in the east marching for Stratholme. Hoping to join up with them and perhaps ending this madness and scourge that has befallen the North. Perhaps the paladins will prove a powerful weapon in this fight.

Page 8.

We could not believe our eyes when we arrived in Stratholme, the city was set ablaze and those we encountered said that the crown prince of Lordaeron grew mad and set aflame to the city in paranoia. Our commander met with the Sorceress Jaina Proudmoore, daughter of the Kul Tiran king and apprentice to Andromath. We will be sailing west for some reason. I don't know what kind of madness this is but orders are orders. The undead hordes of Lordaeron are growing larger and we wont be able to handle them much longer. Arthas has gone North in his mad quest to slay some sort of "Dreadlord". We'll be heading to a port near Capital city to sail past Maelstrom. Some men thought about deserting our forces but were quickly reminded of what awaited them in the wilds of Lordaeron. I hope alls well in Stromgarde.

Page 9.

We set sail for a land to the west, there's so many citizens.... Hoping to escape the hellfire that they left and I can't blame them for being so hasty to abandon their homeland. Even now news are spreading that the demons have returned to Azeroth to set it ablaze. We have enough supplies to last the massive fleet for a few month. It's a wonder that we were able to gather so much. The land that we leave behind may be the last that we ever do. We know that this is a risk, but we made our choice. I just hope Lady Proudmoore is right and there is a continent to the west which is on no known map. We're counting on finding it soon to keep up the morale.

Page 10.

Landfall! We have made it to what the men are starting to call Kalimdor. But the land is a harsh one, we landed in a Desert which showed few signs of plantlife. We were ordered to move west in a mountainous area to build a fortress and seek out a Oracle. I myself would not trust any peddler of magic, much less in a strange land that has been just discovered. Scouts report that orcs were spotted in the nearby desert that we landed in, having sailed here with human ships. Perhaps they followed us? No matter, if they come for us we'll be able to cast the green savages back into the tides!.

Page 11.

The Orcish Horde, lead by a invidual called Thrall (Calling their Warchief a slave? These Orcs are strange) attacked us. Their forces burned down the fortress to the ground and we were forced to flee into the caverns, many suprises were found in these caverns but in the end we made an uneasy alliance with the Orcs.... I do not know what madness has befallen upon them but the Orcs seem to have the same goal as us. We're being sent North to a forested region to set up a base. I dont trust these orcs but I was made commander recently. I was placed in charge of a expedition force made out of Humans and Orcs alike. I hope we can get this over with quickly before the orcs decide to break their promise and betray us. My brothers were sent on similiar missions, my brother Garadol further up north, and the youngest of us Barrdol was sent east.

Page 12.

We were attacked whilst gathering lumber for our fortress, the assailants were similiar to the High Elves of Silvermoon but their skin were of different shades of purple and they seemed to refuse the use of the arcane. We defeated their forces but were later assailed by much worse enemies. The demons had tracked us to this continent and laid siege to our newly built bases. We barely held out and I had sent a missive to the main force for reinforcements. I had also sent news of the Elven natives which had attacked us to Lady Proudmoore although I am sure they already know of them.

Page 13.

I do not know what is going on in her head but Lady Proudmoore has made yet another unreasonable alliance, this time with these "Night Elves". She has called for our forces to assemble on the tallest mountain on Kalimdor called Mount Hyjal to defend some kind of Tree from the Demons. Although I can recognise magical places and their worth it's still insane. If the elves had their way they would have us all die there. I must follow orders though and I am glad I will be able to rejoin my brothers Garadol and Barrdol.

Page 14.

The defense of Mount Hyjal proved costly, my own brother Barrdol was slain when the demons breached our base. But he fought like ten lions, like a true stromic hero he paid with his life so we could buy time for the elves and their plan. Bit by bit we were beaten back suffering ever greater casaulties assaulted by demons and undead alike we were beaten back to the orcish base and even further until we were near the Elves holy tree. The leader of the Demons, Lord Archimonde I believe he was called fell in battle, we had won the battle and our duty was done. We traveled to a land we would eventually call Dustwallow Marsh and established a city called Theramore. It'll be good to rest our bones. and to lay to rest those we have lost, including Barrdol.

Page 15.

It has been months since the legions defeat, we've had to hunt down any remaining demon forces and it seems the uneasy alliance or well, rather truce persists. The orcs were allowed to build their infernal city in the north which they have started to call Orgrimmar. We've established a working relationship with the Night Elves and have even begun trading with them. I've grown to mingle with many of them and although I disagree with many of them, I have grown to respect them. It's quiet and peaceful for now, and we have regained contact with the Human Kingdoms and the rest of the alliance. It's horrible what happened, Arthas has destroyed Lordaeron and Silvermoon, Dalaran has fallen and I don't even know what's happening to Stromgarde. I hope news reach us soon.

Page 16.

I was suprised by who of all people showed up to Theramore of all people, Lord Admiral Daelin Proudemoore himself. A hero of the alliance, he called for all those who wished revenge upon the Horde and with no suprise many joined them. The Orcish menace has to be wiped out one way or another. This is just putting them out of their misery, my brother Garadol agreed to coming with Daelin's forces when I asked him. Were making plans on attacking Durotar, and we have already taken the Echo Isles. We'll be moving on to Orgrimmar soon to finish the job.

Page 17.

The Orcs beat us back, it seems some sort of abomination, a filthy breed of Ogre and Orc lead the Orcish forces, bolstered by ogres trolls and tauren alike to combat against us. My brother Garadol fell to that blasted brutes hand and we couldn't even retrieve his body. This is a lost cause and we have retreated to Theramore. I wont waste my time on Daelins crusade anymore, I'm getting back to Stromgarde one way or another. And after that to Lordaeron, I will find what happened to my brother Amaran and hopefully lay his spirit to rest.


This was written by Odysseus Bunce, last of House Bunce and the son of Strom.

author: Kazgrim
subject: Succession
content_md:
Harpy feathers littered the blood stained ground. Surrounding Ghrakraz laid countless hewned bodies, their stench made foul by the burning Barrens sun. The gray haired orc clutched at his side, wincing from the pain that brought him to his knees. He knelt there, steadying his breath while his mind raced numbly. This wound was no ordinary cut. He felt the harpy's poison coursing throughout his veins. His vision began to blacken, the world around him engulfing in shadows. A faint voice whispered into his ears, although he strained to listen. The last thing he saw was the dark silhouette of an orc he thought he recognized. The words barely could leave his mouth before a dagger plunged into his stomach. Ghrakraz gasped, giving his last breath before falling to the floor. The mysterious figure stood over him, wiping his blade on the sleeve of his robe. His demonic minion gleed with laughter before tearing the corpse apart.

The sun had set, and the land fell to shadow. All that was left were bones and flesh.

author: Thiccroy
subject: <THE RED FIST> - 1 - "The First Campaign: To Stromgarde!"
content_md:
**<THE RED FIST> CHRONICLES**

 *One*

Following the formation of <THE RED FIST> in the Pig and Whistle of Stormwind's Old Town, the five members, Sir Dolokov, Sir Dvarron, Frederick Thorn, Sir Odysseus Bunce and Sir Joreth, set out toward the North, having met a week and a day later near the statue of Danath Trollbane. Originally planning to meet at the gates themselves, meeting at the statue seemed to be either sub-conscious to the Sons of Strom, or a divine message from the Light.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/600030254626635776/unknown.png)

The days passed, moving through the Tram, the cold hills and mountains of Dun Morogh and into Loch Modan, where they rested at Algaz Station. There, they were met by Sir Aristoxenus, a man who wished to join their Brotherhood. As well as a man called Marius, from the Greysteel Company- who were at the time a criminal organization.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/600048575774195748/unknown.png)

They were both accepted, with Marius being accepted more wearily than Aristoxenus. Unfortunately for them, the Dun Algaz Gauntlet would prove to be almost fatal. Dolokhov, Marius and Sir Dvarron would be cut down- but alive. The Dragonmaw ambush would force them to camp in the tumultuous mountains, after a slightly angered and argumentative vote on what to do with the situation.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/600065842054561840/unknown.png)

The day later, they were joined by Lady Ashlynn, of the Greysteel Company, with great scrutiny from their ranks due to her standing within the criminal organization. They were also joined by a Vincent Denmore, who they accepted due to his neutrality. Together, and with Ashlynn's horse's help, they survived another Gnoll ambush and managed to bring Sir Dvarron, who continued to suffer a great concussion, to Menethil Harbor's Physicians.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/602596808933507092/unknown.png)

However, an argument brewed between the Company and Brotherhood, and soon, Odysseus Bunce burned one of the Company member's, as well as Ashlynn, not fatally, but enough to leave a scar. Reprimanded for this, they planned to move out three days later. As they talked of this, Captain Frederick Thorn was voted in by a majority, and so, the first Captain of the First Campaign came to fruition.

Three days later, partnered up by a Lordaeronian Paladin called Saronam the Truehand, and a mercenary from Southshore called Tevyn, the band of warriors and reclaimers set out north of Menethil Harbor. Near the Thandol Span, they met with Dolokhov's mentor and good friend, Gallegund the Red, a Dwarf Warrior-Smith of the Menethil Order. However, the air grew dark as the Greysteel Company followed them in the rear. At first, their Commander, Tripp Blackmoore, offered to help in their quest, but due to grudges and animosity, the Red Fist voted to decline their offer, and the Company continued over the Span in front of the Red Fist.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/604748135390249040/unknown.png)

Suddenly, battle! Dark Iron saboteurs and crazed zealots came out, shooting at the large group and swinging brimstone, axe, and mace at them! In the thick of battle, as all concentrated on their enemies, Odysseus Bunce, still spiteful and under a deeper influence than simple hate, sent a fireball hurling at the Greysteel Mercenary he had wounded three days prior in the Harbor! Quickly singled out, the wounded were tended to and Odysseus captured as a dishonorable traitor to the Red Fist. Knocked out and exorcised of the evil spirit within him by Sir Saronam, he woke up, losing the memories of four years prior- all that happened after the Third War to now.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/604760396016123972/unknown.png)

However.

The Red Fist had done it. They had reached their goal... Their Fatherland.
Stromgarde.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/604771914065510461/unknown.png)

Soon enough, they met with Prince Galen, true Heir to the Throne of Stromgarde. After a lengthy discussion, the Prince gave the Red Fist a home in Stromgarde, a barracks to base their operations in, and the right to have a trial for Odysseus Bunce, as was his right as a noble and now Lord of Stromgarde, due to having come back from distant lands.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/604773536825081884/unknown.png)

The Trial would come the next day. In the Defence stood Dolokhov Steelblood and Odysseus Bunce, and in the Prosecution, Tripp Blackmoore and Baltimus, the victim of Odysseus' fireball. After a lengthy trial, it was witnessed that Odysseus had caused the burning of Baltimus twice, in the span of four days. However, it was told by Saronam that he had exorcised a demon from the man, that had influenced Sir Bunce to cause strife amongst the two organizations. However, as the verdict would be said by Prince Galen, Odysseus shot up, and spoke:

"I demand Trial by Combat!"

The Prince and all around the wizard had frozen in place. The prince allowed it, with a smirk, but was quite bored that so many had volunteered and the two parties had not chosen a champion. So, in an ironic twist, he had chosen randomly for the Defendant and Prosecutor to fight each other.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/594951276429836288/605126856261369943/unknown.png)

The Battle began and quickly turned into DOlokhov's favor, and soon, he was about to kill Blackmoore with a swift, downward strike at the back of his neck! Then, Odysseus and Saronam stopped the duel, and Odysseus quickly pleaded to the outraged Prince to not punish them, but him. So, as everyone else left the Hall of the Chapel to tend to the two wounded champions, they heard screams, and soon, Odysseus Bunce had become one without hands...

TO BE CONTINUED.

subject: The Elven Weaponsmith - <Wayfarers>
content_md:
**Blade of Armistice**

 **Clang! Clang! Clang!**

The familiar sound of the blacksmiths anvil echoed throughout the camp, the keen shriek of metal hammering metal. Seemingly satisfied with her latest addition to the horses shoe collection Elyias stepped back, stooping a ladle in a nearby barrel of water. Drinking deep as she looked around her workspace, her eyes catching the old leather bound tome sitting at her table before she found the forge as its coals seemed to begin cooling.

With a roar, fire spurted free from a layering of fresh coals after each waft of air from the bellows. Satisfied the heat would keep, Elyias swathed a rag over her brow, breathing deeply in the cold night air.

Again her eyes met her tome, as if it was calling to her, begging her for the attention it desired.

Enough was enough she thought as she stormed towards the old book, lifting it with ease as she turned on heel and paced her way to the high table of the camp. Slamming the tome down was a bellow of dust as papers flew into the air. Met only by the eventual creak of the wooden table.

 **“I have something to show you.”** Elyias gleamed, clearly about to enjoy herself as she looked at Lornna’s exemplified shock as her organised chaos was completely shattered by the Elf.

Grinning as she pulls the leather binding from it and sending the pages flying, her hand flying down onto the now open schematic the pages seem to have flown to on their own. With a slight push of the book in Lornna’s direction she spoke again.

 **"There !"** The elf proclaimed, thrusting her hands over the parchment, an extended index tracing over her design. Elyias would trace over an intricate schematic, a blade of exceptional design and beauty, notches seemingly cut out of one side of the blade while the other came to a shallow edge and both met at a distinct point.

![Image](https://scontent-lhr3-1.xx.fbcdn.net/v/t1.0-9/36468808_669193883422535_6270942321366269952_n.jpg?_nc_cat=103&_nc_oc=AQnaPbXROjzgckyJLm2IMGDKiap1R8QnE_UGkBSFeNisvY6Q26f6mnVGyxYhjdmYup8yIH3PIP1nPslRW3P6n06U&_nc_ht=scontent-lhr3-1.xx&oh=08985b72149507b43d92355d3090cabd&oe=5DDF11BC)

 **“I need volunteers. This could be the first of many, but I need the material Lornna! I can’t do this on my own and you have the numbers to help me.”**

 **"This is what I need to bring it together."** Her finger following the design to a list of rather unusual ingredients.

The Elf would turn on heel, tearing a piece of parchment from her journal as she did. After a few steps over to Merrygold's wagon she plunges the dagger through the parchment and into the painted wood of the cart.

"If any of you out there are interested in a little adventure, this is a list of what I need!" Her tone would forever emphasise how unimpressed she seemed with the lack of mobility around camp, turning around back to her forge as she spoke again.

"You know where to find me if you want to volunteer! Think about it- I can't guarantee your safety, but Lornna can at least guarantee the pay!"

 **For those of the Wayfarers that would like a series of side-quests to both improve the functions around camp and if you're lucky improve the very weapons you wield, give us some things to do during downtime and to promote a little more hustle and bustle around camp! So! Either seek me out IC on Elyias or get in touch on the Discord and sign yourself up for what will be one in a long line of mini-quests to come!**

subject: Re: The Elven Weaponsmith - <Wayfarers>
content_md:
Indeed! The material list is custom for RP only!

To give a deeper insight into this, I'll give away the list for this particular acquisition.

 1x Stone heart of a Basilisk broodmother

As many litres as possible of Basilisk blood. (Enough to partially fill a quenching trough)

 1x Essence of a living creature or element

This is the first start towards making a variety of weapons for Roleplay purposes, so that people can gain a fun and interactive prop for both personal and story progression in their own characters.

Each weapon given and created will come with its own description, backstory and a detailed description of the magical properties imbued on it.

((Hope you all enjoy and eventually given the numbers of people who enjoy this idea I'm open for business to more than just the wayfarers!))

subject: <The Greysteel Company> Chapter Four - The Entropy of Truth
content_md:
**[ Chapter Four - The Entropy of Truth ]**
[Authored by John]
 -
As black smoke rose into the skies of Duskwood few noticed.  The sunlight had already been blocked out long ago by foul magic leaving the darkness to envelop what had been the dreams of many.  The Grey Raven tavern had been the base of a local mercenary company but was no longer.  Its captain, a man by the name of Tripp Blackmoore had decided to “cut his losses” with the group he previously called his friends. He left them to burn in the tavern they had all built together.  His plan did not succeed however as he raced into the night, the company had survived, but a long road lay ahead of them.
 -
Their march was not a solemn one, characterised by hunger, exhaustion and loss.  This was a retreat from the world each of them knew.  The communities around the countryside of Stormwind while not always on their side had been their home since the company’s founding.  Expeditions had taken them North in the past, but this was nothing by comparison.   Some were driven by hate, hatred of the leader who had abandoned them, but they all carried with them a slither of hope.  Hope that better times were over the horizon.
 -
On their arrival the great Thane of Dun Garok provided these supplicants the aid they needed.  Shelter, food and fresh water.  While the company was grateful for the aid Thane Gallegund had provided, he tempered his offer with a humble truth of the world.  He would allow them to gather their strength, but after they had done so, the company would need to pay for any further goods or assistance.  It was fair offer the Greysteels accepted, after all, they had no one else to turn to.
 -
 **[ The Sullen Messenger ]**
 -
Even before the Greysteels had arrived the Thane had been receiving troubling news from the surrounding countryside.  The serenity of Hillsbrad Foothills only masked the mystery bubbling beneath its skin.  Rumours of disappearances all across Hillsbrad led the Thane to dispatch one of his trusted scouts to discover the truth, and the evidence Belegar found only made matters more concerning.
 -
Belegar returned to Dun Garok with a furrowed brow and eyes darting across the surroundings.  The rumours had been true.  Farmhands and merchants from all across the region had been disappearing in the night.  Farms understaffed, shops laid bare and scared townspeople the only clues.  The Thane was rightly concerned.  Whatever was happening to these people remained a mystery, but he decided informing the Greysteels would be the correct form of action.  After all, he couldn’t collect payment from them if they disappeared too.
 -
The Thane briefed the Greysteels in the open air of Hillsbrad and while he spoke the man who would help unravel this mystery approached the fortress.  His robes once white, now darkened with blood.  Clutching a sealed letter the guards called for medical assistance however the Greysteels, hearing the commotion arrived first.  James Harvey the Greysteel Doctor attended to the man, but Harvey knew as did the man that he was not long for this world.  Pressing the sealed envelope into Harvey’s hands he spoke his final words.
“H-Hillsbrad……F-F-Fields…..Ma….Ma……..”
With that the wounded man’s strength failed. He was gone.
 -
Opening the letter confused the company even further.  Although the man had given his life to see it delivered it was completely blank.  Handing the letter to Ashlynn Hope she too found it blank, but looking at the now broken seal confirmed the dead man’s words.  It was the seal of Hillsbrad Fields.  With a newfound desire to uncover the reasons behind this man’s actions the Greysteel Company set off to find the truth.
 -
 **[ The Village of Dreams ]**
 -
As the company arrived at the frontier town of Hillsbrad Fields they noticed all was not as it seemed.  Villager and townsfolk were going about their daily business but each one of the Greysteels developed a headache.  They felt that something surrounding the atmosphere of the town was wrong this drove them ever onwards.
 -
Using the description of the deceased man and the broken seal the Greysteels successfully questioned the townspeople.  They discovered that the man was the local priest, going by the name of Gregor.  None who they talked to remembered him leaving, only that he was gone.  The wax seal was confirmed to be that of the aging Town Magistrate, Markus Burnside.  To question him was their next objective, in town hall of Hillsbrad Fields was where they would find him, but getting in proved to be a challenge in of itself.
 -
The guards at the entrance of the town hall were less than helpful.  No matter what the Greysteels said they demanded proof of an appointment.  Orthios DeVarus attempted to use his Argent Dawn connections but it did little to sway the guards.  When they pressed for where to get this appointment the Greysteels discovered that here bureaucracy knew no bounds.  To get an appointment to see the Magistrate, one needed to see his assistant, Susan.  To see his assistant you also needed an appointment.  While the Greysteels were left fuming over this catch-22 Susan was leaving the town hall.  Seeing the commotion she took the Greysteels further away from the guards and heard their plea.
 -
Susan was a kind woman who understood the headache those guards gave everyone.  She believed that they only kept people away from her because they were jealous, but that was neither here nor there.  She was distraught when she heard of Gregor’s death and concerned when she saw the broken seal.  She knew Gregor spoke with the Magistrate before he left the town, it had been that very morning.  Susan mentioned how this friction between the two began when the Magistrate handed out ornate pocket watches to notable citizens.  She mentioned how people were acting differently after they accepted this gift.  She didn’t know where the Magistrate had gotten them.  Her only additional comment was, that the Magistrate wore the only golden watch.  With a similar desire to find out why this happened to Gregor she wrote the Greysteels the legal documents required to see the Magistrate, signing her name at the bottom.
 -
When the entrance guards saw the Greysteels returning they were mid-sentence dictating that they “Get lost!” when they were presented with the proof of appointment.  Shocked by this new development the guards’ faces went white and immediately let them past.  Even calling them “Sir” and “Ma’am”.
 -
The meeting with the Magistrate did not develop as they had hoped.  Without any political tact the Greysteels gave away all the knowledge they had discovered to the Magistrate.  Despite having all the cards they needed, they were left with no option when the Magistrate demanded to see this letter.  As the Magistrate accepted the letter from the Greysteels his other hand rested inside his pocket, the pocket where the golden pocket watch ticked.  The Magistrate burnt the letter in front of the group stating that they “Had nothing”.  Incensed, Caleth Levitt fired his pistol at him.  “GUARDS!” The Magistrate yelled, a battle ensued.
 -
During the course of the battle the two town hall guards were killed by Talvik Giselher and Danwell McDurn.  While Talvik and Danwell dealt with the guards Caleth, Harvey, Ashlynn and Orthios assaulted the Magistrate.  Although no blow injured the Magistrate, when Caleth pulled the Magistrate’s pocket watch away from him he promptly fell to the ground, eyes closed.  With the Greysteels rushing out of the building, no one checked if he was still alive.
 -
As they left the town hall they noticed night was beginning to fall and none of the townsfolk remained outside.  It was at this moment, Caleth opened the golden pocket watch.
 -
Visions shot through Caleth’s mind as he held the watch.  A river leading north.  A fortress on the lake.  The eyes of the man who from that fortress schemed.
 -
The pocket watch burnt into nothing releasing smoke that reformed into the image of a man.  This man was adorned with yellow and blue robes of the light.  This man was familiar to the Greysteels.  Not for his knowledge of the light however, but for his knowledge of the dark.  It was John.  John, the mentor of Ashlynn’s shadow power.  John, the man whom Blackmoore had called a traitor before his own betrayal.  This was different however.  Gone were his scars from shadow magic.  He looked healthier than any of them had seen him before.  He was a new man.
 -
“Murdering guards, assaulting officials.  The only sentence for such crimes is….death.”
As he spoke three men marched in unison in front of the group.  Their eyes were dull, their movements were jagged.  These men were not individuals, they were puppets.
“Goodbye.”
John stated as he flickered out of existence.  And then, the puppets attacked.
 -
The fight was a long and challenging one.  The puppets knew no pain, no fear, they only continued their onslaught until they were dead.  Much like the undead of the Scourge, but these things, however devoid of personality, were still living.  During the battle Caleth distinguished himself as a trick shooter, managing to drop both his pistols and still hit the enemies with their shots.
 -
As the battle drew to a close and the last puppet was killed the Greysteels were left exhausted and wounded.  They returned to Dun Garok to recuperate with some of the knowledge they sought, but with the situation going from bad to worse.  John had returned.
 -
 **[ The Prophet’s Crusade ]**
 -
During the time the Greysteels were recuperating, Belegar had been sent out to scout for any developments since their foray into Hillsbrad Fields.  When he returned, he showed how the situation had deteriorated even further.
 -
Belegar arrived back to Dun Garok steadying himself with his rifle.  It was easy to see what was wrong.  During his scouting mission he had been attacked by “some crazies” as he put it, one of which was a fire mage.  This mage had blown his arm off.  With the Thane currently indisposed he gave his report to the Greysteels while their Doctor bandaged the stump he once called an arm.
 -
The scout spoke of whole Syndicate Outposts being empty, the only clue being their emblems lying on the ground.  While an outpost being empty would normally be cause for celebration the presence of their emblems made it only concerning.  Syndicate members are executed for losing their emblem.  Why would they just drop theirs and walk off?  A sudden change of heart or something sinister?  He spoke of groups like the one that attacked him coming down from the north via Hillsbrad River.  He spoke of town stockades being found empty, not even the guards were found.  He spoke of a militia arriving in Hillsbrad Fields who would attack anyone who came near.  Finally before his report was over, he warned the Greysteels not to attack any large group, even with them united he did not see them triumphing.
 -
It was in this moment Caleth shared the visions he received from the pocket watch.  Although annoyed by not sharing his knowledge sooner, the Greysteels set off for the fortress on the lake.  Caer Darrow.  It was there they believed they would find John.  There they believed they could stop this madness.
 -
Travelling up Hillsbrad River they found the sites mentioned in the Dwarf’s report.  Even the spot where he was attacked, but it was not until they entered the Western Plaguelands and reached the bridge to Caer Darrow did they find a group like the one that had attacked Belegar.
 -
Just as they suspected it was a group of John’s puppets, but this was much larger than before.  Organised into two columns of five the group numbered ten puppets, each with the same ferocity of the three that attacked them in Hillsbrad Fields.  Shocked into inaction the Greysteels failed to react before the group of puppets had spotted them.  As they readied a volley to kill the Greysteels, Caleth used a smoke grenade to break line of sight.  As line of sight was broken the Greysteels ran like never before.  They ran and hid, there was no other option.  They struggled against three.  Ten would be their end.
 -
Thankfully the puppets soon resumed their march south, leaving the bridge unoccupied.  Moving across the bridge the Greysteels found only one guarding the entrance to Caer Darrow.  Although he was covered in runes seemingly burnt onto his skin they assumed they could take him.  He was only one man.  It was the hardest fight yet.
 -
Almost killing Talvik in one swing of his sword this man could only be described as an elite guard.  A Praetorian Guard.  Almost all perishing without landing a single blow it was the quick thinking of Aristoxenus Makrelis tackling and disarming the Praetorian that gave the Greysteels more time.  To kill him Ashlynn Hope used her shadow magic to overload the Praetorian’s smouldering runes, weakening him enough for the rest of the Greysteels to kill him.  With the Praetorian Guard lying dead the Greysteels entered the Fortress of Caer Darrow.
 -
It was here, in the ruins they found John.  Standing in front of a huge statue of a pious man he was waiting for them.
 -
“I must admit I am surprised to see you all here.  With how badly you normally perform I expected you all to die on the way.  Alas, you have instead murdered all the people who tried to stop you.  The people whom had saved.  Don’t you feel guilty?”
 -
“You do not understand, but I set them free.  Free from freedom, responsibility, thoughts.  This is the next step.  Evolution.  Before I saved them these people they were murderers, rapists and traitors.  Some struggled to find food, others struggled with their own feelings.  Now they struggle no longer. Now they know peace. Who can deny the people this improvement?”
 -
“Initially I thought only to influence people into the right direction.  Force truth into their thoughts but otherwise leave them.  I must thank you and Gregor for showing me how unfeasible that was. You showed that while there are still those who are outside my grip, there will always be those who cannot fathom what we could achieve.  Tell me Greysteels, don’t you too long for a world without war?”
 -
“I once dreamed of it, believing it unattainable.  Now I reach ever closer towards it, the inevitable ticking of clockwork.  You can’t fight evolution.  Did the lungfish refuse to breathe air? No. It dragged itself forth from the blackest ocean abyss, leaving its brethren, with lidless eyes forever staring at the dark.  Doomed despite eternal vigilance.  I have taken that first breathe, but I will not abandon you all. I offer you redemption, I offer you freedom, you need only reach out and accept it.”
 -
With that last statement he held out a golden pocket watch, offering it to the Greysteels.  Rejecting the gift they perceived as a poison chalice, Harvey began the attack, using his wand to send a fire bolt at John.
 -
John fought with rays of light, exhausting the minds and bodies of the Greysteel Company.  This was unlike they had ever seen John.  They knew of a man who wielded shadow magic to pursue his goals, not this man before them.  Ashlynn was so shocked by John’s change didn’t react as he defended himself from the rest of the Greysteels.  All seemed lost as John dodged every blow while inflicting massive damage on the group.  Talvik however, saw through the rays of light.  After being knocked into exhaustion by John he analysed the situation before him.  The light had no feeling behind it, it was in all sense of the word, empty.  John’s body shimmered at the edges.  It was then he realised.  It was all an illusion.
 -
 **[ The Truth Revealed ]**
 -
The spell over his mind broken he rose to his feet declaring this truth to the rest of the group.  Enraged the Avatar of John attempted to lash out at Talvik, but to no avail.  The Avatar disintegrated as did his spell over the Greysteel Company.
 -
The Greysteels entered Caer Darrow Keep with newfound resolve to find John.  They had defeated his illusion, they would now defeat him.
 -
What they found was a shadow, a husk of what John used to be.  Clutching an orb of seething shadows, sitting in the top room of the keep.  Surrounded by medicine his skin was grey and he looked gaunt.  He only had the strength to utter a few words.
“How could you….All my work…..”
With that his skin began to fall off, his very essence was being drained into the Orb he clutched with his bony fingers.  It took no time at all for the process to be complete.
 -
John was gone, only a skeleton of the man remained, still clutching that hateful Orb.
 -
When the Greysteels approached it they began to fight over who would take it.  It was clear the Orb was affecting their minds.  A battle between each member of the company began.  Friend against friend, the dance to the Orb’s tune.
 -
After Ashlynn and Caleth were knocked unconscious by their compatriots Harvey handed the Orb to Talvik.  Talvik believed that destroying the Orb would free the world of its torment.  As he broke open the Orb, the darkness was released into the world.  What had he done?
 -
 **[ Epilogue ]**
 -
 **Susan**
Blamed for the attack on the Magistrate and his guards by letting <The Greysteel Company> in she was arrested, standing trial for manslaughter and treason.  Forgotten by <The Greysteel Company> she was promptly found guilty.  She wept as they took her to the gallows.
 -
 **Magistrate Burnside**
Having the connection between his mind and the watch broken so violently, he fell into a coma.  He never woke up.
 -
 **Army of John the Prophet**
With the death of John, the personalities of those controlled by him returned en masse.  Tormented within the Eye some lost their minds, those who didn’t took their anger out on the Town John forced them to protect.  The smoke from Hillsbrad Fields could be seen from miles around.
 -
 **Gregor**
None remembered Gregor as the dutiful priest he was.  Most who knew him died at the Massacre of Hillsbrad Fields.  Despite sacrificing himself to find those to save the town, he failed, his name was lost to time.
 -
 **Belegar**
Honourably discharged from his military career due to injury he settled down in Ironforge where he found himself a true Dwarvish wife.  The very nurse who tendered to his wounds.
 -
 **John**
Caleth returned to Caer Darrow, burying the bones of John somewhere in the Western Plaguelands.  He marked the grave with the name “Old Man”.

Some struggled to find food, others struggled with their own feelings. Now they struggle no longer. Now they know peace. Who can deny the people this improvement?”
-
“Initially I thought only to influence people into the right direction. Force truth into their thoughts but otherwise leave them. I must thank you and Gregor for showing me how unfeasible that was. You showed that while there are still those who are outside my grip, there will always be those who cannot fathom what we could achieve. Tell me Greysteels, don’t you too long for a world without war?”
-
“I once dreamed of it, believing it unattainable. Now I reach ever closer towards it, the inevitable ticking of clockwork. You can’t fight evolution. Did the lungfish refuse to breathe air? No. It dragged itself forth from the blackest ocean abyss, leaving its brethren, with lidless eyes forever staring at the dark. Doomed despite eternal vigilance. I have taken that first breathe, but I will not abandon you all. I offer you redemption, I offer you freedom, you need only reach out and accept it.”
-
With that last statement he held out a golden pocket watch, offering it to the Greysteels. Rejecting the gift they perceived as a poison chalice, Harvey began the attack, using his wand to send a fire bolt at John.
-
John fought with rays of light, exhausting the minds and bodies of the Greysteel Company. This was unlike they had ever seen John. They knew of a man who wielded shadow magic to pursue his goals, not this man before them. Ashlynn was so shocked by John’s change didn’t react as he defended himself from the rest of the Greysteels. All seemed lost as John dodged every blow while inflicting massive damage on the group. Talvik however, saw through the rays of light. After being knocked into exhaustion by John he analysed the situation before him. The light had no feeling behind it, it was in all sense of the word, empty. John’s body shimmered at the edges. It was then he realised. It was all an illusion.
-
[ The Truth Revealed ]
-
The spell over his mind broken he rose to his feet declaring this truth to the rest of the group. Enraged the Avatar of John attempted to lash out at Talvik, but to no avail. The Avatar disintegrated as did his spell over the Greysteel Company.
-
The Greysteels entered Caer Darrow Keep with newfound resolve to find John. They had defeated his illusion, they would now defeat him.
-
What they found was a shadow, a husk of what John used to be. Clutching an orb of seething shadows, sitting in the top room of the keep. Surrounded by medicine his skin was grey and he looked gaunt. He only had the strength to utter a few words.
“How could you….All my work…..”
With that his skin began to fall off, his very essence was being drained into the Orb he clutched with his bony fingers. It took no time at all for the process to be complete.
-
John was gone, only a skeleton of the man remained, still clutching that hateful Orb.
-
When the Greysteels approached it they began to fight over who would take it. It was clear the Orb was affecting their minds. A battle between each member of the company began. Friend against friend, the dance to the Orb’s tune.
-
After Ashlynn and Caleth were knocked unconscious by their compatriots Harvey handed the Orb to Talvik. Talvik believed that destroying the Orb would free the world of its torment. As he broke open the Orb, the darkness was released into the world. What had he done?
-
[ Epilogue ]
-
Susan
Blamed for the attack on the Magistrate and his guards by letting <The Greysteel Company> in she was arrested, standing trial for manslaughter and treason. Forgotten by <The Greysteel Company> she was promptly found guilty. She wept as they took her to the gallows.
-
Magistrate Burnside
Having the connection between his mind and the watch broken so violently, he fell into a coma. He never woke up.
-
Army of John the Prophet
With the death of John, the personalities of those controlled by him returned en masse. Tormented within the Eye some lost their minds, those who didn’t took their anger out on the Town John forced them to protect. The smoke from Hillsbrad Fields could be seen from miles around.
-
Gregor
None remembered Gregor as the dutiful priest he was. Most who knew him died at the Massacre of Hillsbrad Fields. Despite sacrificing himself to find those to save the town, he failed, his name was lost to time.
-
Belegar
Honourably discharged from his military career due to injury he settled down in Ironforge where he found himself a true Dwarvish wife. The very nurse who tendered to his wounds.
-
John
Caleth returned to Caer Darrow, burying the bones of John somewhere in the Western Plaguelands. He marked the grave with the name “Old Man”.

subject: Quest in a tabern. Cap 3
content_md:
The Twilight's Hammer has moved into the Moonshrine Ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. Their presence can only serve to coerce the elements into working against the Horde. If left unchecked, Ashenvale will be theirs for good.

They asked me to go into Blackfathom and find the ruin's fathom stone; it should be somewhere close in the water. In it is a fathom core - a device that when properly read it will relate a history of all elemental activity. If I recover it, my contact and the Earthen Ring can maybe do something to stop them!

Join me, for freedom, join me for the Horde.

Mirta

author: Draconis
subject: On the matter of the Silithid, a report about the new species in Kalimdor.
content_md:
**KC 617(1): 22-30**

New species and reports of Silithids (Silithida) and Qiraji from Kalimdor

A.Thomas Matheny 1, Daryn Lightwind 2 & Mae Paledust 3

 1 Knightly Order of the Silver Hand, Expeditionary Command of the Western Alliance, Theramore.

 2 Druidic Order of the Cenarion Circle, Lorekeeper of the Order, Darnassus.

 3 Archeological League of the Explorers, Historian of the Guild, Ironforge.

 **Summary**

A.Thomas Matheny, Daryn Lightwind & Mae Paledust. 617. New species and reports of ***Silithids*** (Silithida) and ***Qiraji*** from Kalimdor.

Following up on recent developments concerning disappearances of passengers to and from the southern side of the continent of Kalimdor over the months of March to September, under leadership of appointed expeditionary leader Aurelian Thomas Matheny of the Knightly Order of the Silver Hand, with authorization from the ruling body of the city-state of Theramore, a small group of recruited explorers and combatants explored areas: The Field of Giants (Southern Barrens), The Shimmering Flats (Eastern Thousand Needles), for more information on reported sightings and disappearances.

Having found sufficient evidence of a nearly parasitic species of insectoid creatures, dubbed the Silithid by our Kaldorei associates, with the aid of senior Lorekeeper Lightwind and Historian Paledust, I present this report to the governing bodies of the Alliance, and the higher chains of Command.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/PxQPJhY/Silithids01.jpg)
 *Pictured above is a collection of sketches of several types of these creatures, including castes: Tunneler, Wasp, Reaver. (From left to right.)*

 **The Silithids**

A species of as of now unknown origins, the Silithid are an insectoid race primarily found in the continent of Kalimdor, their native territory being that of the desert of Silithus in the south-western region of the continent.

Recently however, they have been shown to be versatile in surviving both milder regions, such as the southern Barrens, as well as the more humid regions of the forests of Feralas on the western coast of the continent.

The primary tool of this species is adaptation. It seems to satisfy the need of the hive, or colony in particular, the most obvious example of this would be the color of their outer body. A shell like construct which acts as armor for the species. In dry regions, the following colors have been noted: Turquoise Teal, Flax Yellow, Ruby Red. (Current information indicates the choice of color in these regions is primarily for one of two functions, camouflage to hide from potential threats, or bright colors to insinuate danger to said threats.)

In humid regions, the following colors have been noted: Turquoise Teal, Jade Green. (Current information indicates adaptation to the humid environment for better concealment in plain sight among foliage and shrubbery.)

No creature yet encountered, has shown the ability of swift adaptation to changes in the environment as the Silithid have. Caste Larvae, more commonly referred to as Broodlings, can evolve into a variety creature types based on the needs of the hive. Estimations show less than a month is required for a newly hatched Broodling to fully mature under calm circumstances and based on previous information about insectoid creatures, it is estimated an average lifespan is 5 to 10 years.

On the matter of scale, Silithid can range from the size of a normal insect, to gigantic in proportions. (See later Caste Colossi for more information.)  Estimations show the size of a fully grown Silithid varies on the period of time that it is allowed to develop in their egg stage. Current information also links size to the size of the colony of origination. A large number of Castes usually surpass human scale.

On the matter of appearance, Silithid range depending on caste, but all share several key parts. Each Silithid shares insectoid like features, antennae which pertrude from their head region, act as a means of communication, coordination and receiving information. Chemical dispersion into the air may also be critical in this. (Currently unconfirmed, requires further analysis.)

While numerous, they do not appear to be capable of intelligent and individual action. The antennae serve as a radio antenna for a transmission from afar. (A presumed Hivemind?) Every action of the Hive, and in turn every colony is as follows, directed towards a singular goal, the extinction and consumption of non-Silithid organisms.
On the matter of origin, several theories propose a link between these Silithid and the Nerubians of the Scourge. (Currently unconfirmed, requires more data.) Kaldorei colleges propose a link between the Silithid and the Qiraji. (See Qiraji further in the report for more information.)

On the matter of reproduction, Silithid life begins as an egg, most likely spawned from a Broodmother like caste and attached to colony walls as to allow more calm growth and further securing already established taint of the land the colony inhabits.

From an egg is born Caste Larvae, at this point a broodling and unspecialized for any particular role in Silithid society. Eventually, the broodling encases itself in a cocoon and changes into a new form. (See Castes for more information.)
On the matter of habitat, it seems as of now they prefer a combination of dry and arid landscape, along with deeper sub-terrain tunnels. Silithid colonies, dubbed Hives, are massive in scale, and usually surrounded by a combination of natural materials produced from Silithid bodily secretions and towering antenna-like spires jutting out of the earth. In the maze of tunnels below the surface, the Silithid raise their young, tend to their wounded, manage stores of food and water and gather to fend off hostile threats.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/68n9NBH/Silithid-Hive01.jpg)
 *Pictured above is area designated: Noxius Lair (Tanaris.)*

On the matter of diet, current research indicates all biological mass is edible to the Silithid, using it they in turn are able to produce more of their kind, and continue their evolutionary cycle. Research also indicates rock is within their edible pallet. No current indication shows they are capable of eating metals or stronger materials, however visible analysis shows attempts to dilute the sturdier material with an ooze like substance have been attempted.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/1mxynwM/Silithid-Metal01.jpg)
 *Pictured above is a taken photograph of an ooze covered vein of the metal: Mithril. Its natural shined enhanced by the odd liquid, and the metal itself seems untainted in any way, further analysis is required.*

Due to inhabiting arid regions, current research suggests a large quantity of water is required to fuel the ever growing swarm. Large gatherings of Silithid near water rich areas of Tanaris, indicate it is crucial to their continued growth.

On the matter of hostility, while smaller sized Silithid seemed more pre-occupied with handling matters of hive construction and preservation, certain castes of the Silithid are utterly devoted to the cause of combat and extermination. Furthermore, Kaldorei historical data provides insight on a conflict dubbed, The War of the Shifting Sands. (Currently seeking out more information on this conflict.) When given the order, tens of thousands of Silithid can be mobilized within days, and sent out to attack nearly any position where their tunnels can dig into. It is also highlighted that for every fifty that fall, another hundred are already prepared to take their place going off of Kaldorei records. By contrast to similar incursions (See reports on Scourge and Demons for more information), the goal of the Silithid is not the simple extermination of all non-Silithid races, but the consumption of their entire beings for furthering the cause of Silithid evolution, at any cost.
On the matter of society, the Silithid society has been organized into several different castes, with differing physical types. Every caste has its unique function within their society, though all share objectives of expanding living quarters for future generations as well as the defense of the younger and vurnrable larvae and eggs.

 **Castes**

 **Caste Larvae – Broodlings.**

Silithid Larvae, also known as Broodlings, are young silithid that as of yet have not been specialized for any role in the hive. Eventually they encase themselves in a cocoon and change into a new form depending on the needs of the Hive.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/rGDSjr6/Silithids02.jpg) ![Image](https://i.ibb.co/MDCfTYJ/Silithids02-5.jpg)
 *Pictured above are the two stages of a larva, above after having hatched, and below in their cocoon, slowly evolving into a new creature.*

They represent one of the most numerous castes of Silithid, and also one of the least aggressive. (Likely underdeveloped senses.)

 **Caste Light – Illuminators.**

Consisting of two species, named Lights and Pill bugs. The Illuminators act as nearly undeveloped larva in many ways, but their primary function is the illumination of the mazes of tunnels which make up the many hives, usually found clinging to walls, floors or ceilings. They show no aggressiveness even in close proximity to non-Silithid species.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/fnZdht0/Silithids03.jpg)
 *Image of a Light, their lighting capabilities originate from a glow source at the back of their bodies.*

Current numbers are unknown, but current estimations show a single Hive can possess from a few dozen to several hundred.

 **Caste Worker – Tunnelers.**

The Worker caste consists of four primary creature types, Workers, Tunnelers, Swarmers and Scarabs.
While similar, evidence shows a clear separation.

Workers primarily maintain the Hives themselves, constructing large towering spires, and seeing to the preservation of eggs and larva.

Tunnelers dig out ever spanning and far reaching cavernous pathways through which the large Silithid swarms can maneuver.

Scarabs act as the large levy force of the Silithid, being the most numerous of any caste, the footmen of their species, they are usually found guarding the outside of a Hive.

Swarmers act as a veteran sergeants for the Silithid, commanding many Scarabs to follow them into combating hostile threats, eliminating them early is likely to cause confusion or even a break of their swarm.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/rHRCMzp/Silithids04.jpg)
 *Pictured above is a Swarmer, nearly all members of this Caste grow to human height, and the width of an orc.*

 **Caste Wasp – Flyers.**

Silithid Wasps make up the aerial force of the Silithid, a mobile army always ruthlessly defending the Hive even until death, going into suicidal assaults simply to protect their own. They possess a large pair of insectoid wings allowing for impressive speeds and noise. Records indicate the noise of a squadron of Wasps is capable of being heard up to a kilometer away from their current position. While they do possess legs with which to perch themselves, they seem to serve no real combat purpose.

For weapons, they have evolved to use incredibly sharp nearly sword like claw limbs, and a large wasp like stinger, some Silithid within the region of Feralas have even developed an affinity for using venom to quickly take down even the most difficult of opponents. Swarm tactics are their primary means of combat.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/Z66YW6G/Silithids05.jpg)
 *Pictured above is a Wasp, a total wingspan is capable of reaching 3 meters in distance.*

 **Caste Reaver – Warriors.**

According to Kaldorei records, the primary fighting force of the Silithid is made up of Reavers, more humorously named ‘Battle Tanks’ by our Dwarven collegues. Their near vehicle like armor, horse like speed, and incredible strength make them the near perfect combatants.

While Scarabs defend the outside of the Hive, the primary defense of the inner hallways are left to the Reavers, who using their developed nightvision are capable of seeing even the most careful of infiltrators. Defensive in nature, they will rarely be persuaded into battle unfavorable for them, and will never advance past a position deemed necessary. With a weight easily going over 160 kilograms, their full charge combined with their thick exoskeleton allows for devastating penetrations through enemy lines.

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/RvDTxwx/Silithis06.jpg)
 *Pictured above is a Reaver, patrolling the inner tunnels of a Hive.*

 **Currently researched Castes.**

The following castes are mentioned in name or in short description by our Kaldorei collegues, any further information is unknown:

 **Caste Queen**

Broodmothers of the Swarm, primary purpose is the laying of eggs.

 **Caste Colossi**

The largest of the Silithid, living battering rams for the swarm, they provide a means to combat larger foes when the many legions of the Swarm are unable. Records indicate monstrous growth of nearly 8 or 10 meters, armed with scythe like appendixes and near indestructible exoskeleton.

 **Caste Sand Reaver**

A potential variation on either the Tunnelers or Reavers, Sand Reavers seem to serve as larger tunnel  diggers.

 **Caste Statue**

While not Silithid themselves, Kaldorei records indicate the usage of two kinds of constructs in battle similar to Dwarven Golems, these are the Anubisaths and Obsidian Destroyers.

Anubisaths are described as towering stone constructs of immense physical might, capable of even downing dragons if given the chance. They possess the features of a jackal for a head, and the body of a near humanoid.

Obsidian Destroyers seem to appear in a near centaur like fashion of merging, between a horse and a lion. Their greatest usage is in the nullification and dispersion of magical energies.

 **Qiraji**

Currently not much is known about this secondary species, though unlike the Silithid, they seem to possess individual thought and a capability to act independently of the swarm. Kaldorei records indicate positions of Generals and Commanders of the Swarm, indicating a role of leadership. Whether they are their own caste within the Silithid hierarchy or their own species, is as of this moment unclear.

 **Countermeasures**

Current investigation into a possible way to combat the Swarm reveals a plant known as Morrowgrain, currently being studied by members of the Druidic Order of the Cenarion Circle. (Seek out Archdruid Fandral Staghelm for more information on this research.)

The disruption of antenna is likely to disrupt a connection to a supposed Hivemind, allowing for chaos to spread within Silithid ranks. (As of now, unproven.)

 **Conclusion**

With this information presented, gathered from researching history, biology and geography. I emplore the reader to carefully consider future methods of combating this threat, while preparing for a full on engagement. Recent activity shows that while they were once in a way imprisoned with the sands of Silithus, they have begun to spread and create new Hives all across Southern Kalimdor. It is a threat which cannot be ignored, lest the follies of our past return to haunt us.
 -Sir Aurelian Thomas Matheny, Knight of Theramore.
