In the maze of tunnels below the surface, the Silithid raise their young, tend to their wounded, manage stores of food and water and gather to fend off hostile threats.


Pictured above is area designated: Noxius Lair (Tanaris.)

On the matter of diet, current research indicates all biological mass is edible to the Silithid, using it they in turn are able to produce more of their kind, and continue their evolutionary cycle. Research also indicates rock is within their edible pallet. No current indication shows they are capable of eating metals or stronger materials, however visible analysis shows attempts to dilute the sturdier material with an ooze like substance have been attempted.


Pictured above is a taken photograph of an ooze covered vein of the metal: Mithril. Its natural shined enhanced by the odd liquid, and the metal itself seems untainted in any way, further analysis is required.

Due to inhabiting arid regions, current research suggests a large quantity of water is required to fuel the ever growing swarm. Large gatherings of Silithid near water rich areas of Tanaris, indicate it is crucial to their continued growth.

On the matter of hostility, while smaller sized Silithid seemed more pre-occupied with handling matters of hive construction and preservation, certain castes of the Silithid are utterly devoted to the cause of combat and extermination. Furthermore, Kaldorei historical data provides insight on a conflict dubbed, The War of the Shifting Sands. (Currently seeking out more information on this conflict.) When given the order, tens of thousands of Silithid can be mobilized within days, and sent out to attack nearly any position where their tunnels can dig into. It is also highlighted that for every fifty that fall, another hundred are already prepared to take their place going off of Kaldorei records. By contrast to similar incursions (See reports on Scourge and Demons for more information), the goal of the Silithid is not the simple extermination of all non-Silithid races, but the consumption of their entire beings for furthering the cause of Silithid evolution, at any cost.
On the matter of society, the Silithid society has been organized into several different castes, with differing physical types. Every caste has its unique function within their society, though all share objectives of expanding living quarters for future generations as well as the defense of the younger and vurnrable larvae and eggs.

Castes

Caste Larvae – Broodlings.

Silithid Larvae, also known as Broodlings, are young silithid that as of yet have not been specialized for any role in the hive. Eventually they encase themselves in a cocoon and change into a new form depending on the needs of the Hive.


Pictured above are the two stages of a larva, above after having hatched, and below in their cocoon, slowly evolving into a new creature.

They represent one of the most numerous castes of Silithid, and also one of the least aggressive. (Likely underdeveloped senses.)

Caste Light – Illuminators.

Consisting of two species, named Lights and Pill bugs. The Illuminators act as nearly undeveloped larva in many ways, but their primary function is the illumination of the mazes of tunnels which make up the many hives, usually found clinging to walls, floors or ceilings. They show no aggressiveness even in close proximity to non-Silithid species.


Image of a Light, their lighting capabilities originate from a glow source at the back of their bodies.

Current numbers are unknown, but current estimations show a single Hive can possess from a few dozen to several hundred.

Caste Worker – Tunnelers.

The Worker caste consists of four primary creature types, Workers, Tunnelers, Swarmers and Scarabs.
While similar, evidence shows a clear separation.

Workers primarily maintain the Hives themselves, constructing large towering spires, and seeing to the preservation of eggs and larva.

Tunnelers dig out ever spanning and far reaching cavernous pathways through which the large Silithid swarms can maneuver.

Scarabs act as the large levy force of the Silithid, being the most numerous of any caste, the footmen of their species, they are usually found guarding the outside of a Hive.

Swarmers act as a veteran sergeants for the Silithid, commanding many Scarabs to follow them into combating hostile threats, eliminating them early is likely to cause confusion or even a break of their swarm.


Pictured above is a Swarmer, nearly all members of this Caste grow to human height, and the width of an orc.

Caste Wasp – Flyers.

Silithid Wasps make up the aerial force of the Silithid, a mobile army always ruthlessly defending the Hive even until death, going into suicidal assaults simply to protect their own. They possess a large pair of insectoid wings allowing for impressive speeds and noise. Records indicate the noise of a squadron of Wasps is capable of being heard up to a kilometer away from their current position. While they do possess legs with which to perch themselves, they seem to serve no real combat purpose.

For weapons, they have evolved to use incredibly sharp nearly sword like claw limbs, and a large wasp like stinger, some Silithid within the region of Feralas have even developed an affinity for using venom to quickly take down even the most difficult of opponents. Swarm tactics are their primary means of combat.


Pictured above is a Wasp, a total wingspan is capable of reaching 3 meters in distance.

Caste Reaver – Warriors.

According to Kaldorei records, the primary fighting force of the Silithid is made up of Reavers, more humorously named ‘Battle Tanks’ by our Dwarven collegues. Their near vehicle like armor, horse like speed, and incredible strength make them the near perfect combatants.

While Scarabs defend the outside of the Hive, the primary defense of the inner hallways are left to the Reavers, who using their developed nightvision are capable of seeing even the most careful of infiltrators. Defensive in nature, they will rarely be persuaded into battle unfavorable for them, and will never advance past a position deemed necessary. With a weight easily going over 160 kilograms, their full charge combined with their thick exoskeleton allows for devastating penetrations through enemy lines.


Pictured above is a Reaver, patrolling the inner tunnels of a Hive.

Currently researched Castes.

The following castes are mentioned in name or in short description by our Kaldorei collegues, any further information is unknown:

Caste Queen

Broodmothers of the Swarm, primary purpose is the laying of eggs.

Caste Colossi

The largest of the Silithid, living battering rams for the swarm, they provide a means to combat larger foes when the many legions of the Swarm are unable. Records indicate monstrous growth of nearly 8 or 10 meters, armed with scythe like appendixes and near indestructible exoskeleton.

Caste Sand Reaver

A potential variation on either the Tunnelers or Reavers, Sand Reavers seem to serve as larger tunnel diggers.

Caste Statue

While not Silithid themselves, Kaldorei records indicate the usage of two kinds of constructs in battle similar to Dwarven Golems, these are the Anubisaths and Obsidian Destroyers.

Anubisaths are described as towering stone constructs of immense physical might, capable of even downing dragons if given the chance. They possess the features of a jackal for a head, and the body of a near humanoid.

Obsidian Destroyers seem to appear in a near centaur like fashion of merging, between a horse and a lion. Their greatest usage is in the nullification and dispersion of magical energies.

Qiraji

Currently not much is known about this secondary species, though unlike the Silithid, they seem to possess individual thought and a capability to act independently of the swarm. Kaldorei records indicate positions of Generals and Commanders of the Swarm, indicating a role of leadership. Whether they are their own caste within the Silithid hierarchy or their own species, is as of this moment unclear.

Countermeasures

Current investigation into a possible way to combat the Swarm reveals a plant known as Morrowgrain, currently being studied by members of the Druidic Order of the Cenarion Circle. (Seek out Archdruid Fandral Staghelm for more information on this research.)

The disruption of antenna is likely to disrupt a connection to a supposed Hivemind, allowing for chaos to spread within Silithid ranks. (As of now, unproven.)

Conclusion

With this information presented, gathered from researching history, biology and geography. I emplore the reader to carefully consider future methods of combating this threat, while preparing for a full on engagement. Recent activity shows that while they were once in a way imprisoned with the sands of Silithus, they have begun to spread and create new Hives all across Southern Kalimdor. It is a threat which cannot be ignored, lest the follies of our past return to haunt us.
-Sir Aurelian Thomas Matheny, Knight of Theramore.

author: Casanova
subject: The Congress of TurtleWow Roleplay
content_md:
Community announcement:

We’ve all felt it.
The arrival of Classic and the end of summer holidays.

These two events have changed the TurtleWoW roleplay community.  Sadly, not for the better.  Roleplay Guilds have been disappearing.
Our roleplay community has shrunk.  Smaller?  Yes.  Defeated? No.  We refuse to stand idly by while the roleplay community struggles.  It is time for all the Roleplay Guilds to work together to achieve both larger and higher quality roleplay.

We call for a <Congress of TurtleWoW Roleplay>

This will be an OOC organisation.  Here we will collate all the roleplay systems and lore from different guilds into one place.  Changing from one roleplay system to another will never be easier.  Finding out which guild controls what territory will be simple.  Multi-Guild events will no longer be as much of an organisational nightmare.  Each guild will be autonomous, but connected to others like never before.

The following guilds are already members:
<The Greysteel Company>
<The Crimson Eagle>
<Ghosts of Lordaeron>
<Cenarion Circle>
<Raven Trade Co>
<The Knights Templars>

Will you join our ranks?  Will you join a roleplay organisation that will stand the test of time?  May the future be ours!  Glory to TurtleWoW Roleplay!
<https://discord.gg//nG8n2UR>

<Signed Council Member John on behalf of Council Members Caleth, Talvik and Danwell>

author: Qixel
subject: First Annual Engie Industries Advent Exchange
content_md:
Sitting at her desk, the half-goblin stashed her right hand into her pocket and jangled some gold coins. The sound always helped to focus her, but her mind still wandered - it *was* that time of year again, she supposed. *Clink, clink, clink.* Chin cupped in her left hand, she tapped her cheek absently. *Clink, clink, clink. Tap, tap, tap.*

"Arrrrgh!" She suddenly stood up and ran her fingers frantically through her hair. She looked around her office, desperate for something to distract her. "Stupid, wasteful, pointless!" She muttered angrily as she thought again about the upcoming festivities. More specifically, what she wanted to do. *Didn't want to do!* "No, no, no!" She paced angrily around the room.

Although she prided herself on her goblin heritage, Engie was just as much a gnome, and the jubilant festivities had always enthralled her, whether she liked it or not. And that wouldn't be such a *problem* - indeed, holidays were a fantastic chance to make some gold! - if not for the fact that every year she was overcome by some stupid urge to give stuff away. *For free!* There's no profit in giving away your product!

 *'Everything has a price.'* Those words were both the slogan for her company, as well as the words she lived by. Indeed, everything had a price, be it goods, equipment, or services. And to just.... *give it away*? Uggggh. Her skin crawled at the prospect. And yet, here she was, fighting that exact urge. It was as if she were splitting in two, and each part of herself was warring over what to do.

She screamed in frustration again, then suddenly froze. "Wait. What if I could do both?" She murmured softly. The half-gnome quickly sat back down at her desk and opened a drawer to grab a sheet of paper. The logic was contradictory - to give things away, but to gain a profit in doing so. It was nonsense, but nonsense was often *incredibly* lucrative. A way to satisfy both her gnomish need for jubilant festivities, and her goblin need for some cash.

She grinned. "Yeah, I can do this."

She set about drawing up a poster for the....

 **First Annual Engie Industries Advent Exchange**

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/bKvWMXQ.png)
 *I commissioned this artwork from the marvelous [WI33ARD](https://www.deviantart.com/wi33ard) over at deviantart. <3 Go check him out if ya want! :D*
_________________________________________________________________________________________
What is this? Engie has decided to throw a big, month long party? What has possessed that little half-gnome of such an audacious idea? She normally keeps to herself unless someone is paying her for her company. Could it be Winter Veil festivities on the mind?

Indeed it is. Engie will be giving a free gift away each day of December to those who meet with her, ostensibly in order to advertise her company.

_________________________________________________________________________________________

 **F.A.Q.**

Q: So, your roleplay bits are hard to understand. Can we break character a moment and find out what all this is?
A: Sure. Basically, when I was a kid, I played this game called 'Neopets'. And one of the things I looked forward to every year was the 'Advent Calendar', a little event held in december where you could claim a prize every day. Recently, while I was slaving around as an adult working retail, I remembered the joy from those simpler times, and wanted to share it with everyone here. And thus, the Advent Exchange was conceived.

Q: So you're gonna be giving free stuff?
A: Yup. Although it won't be as well organized as neopets had it, of course. Instead, I've been preparing and will continue to prepare items in wrapped gifts to hand out to people. I'm randomizing them as I do them, too, so even I don't know what's in the gifts anymore! How exciting!

Q: Well, I mean, surely you remember some of the items you wrap. Can you give us some teasers as to what's in the box(es)?
A: Well, equipment of varying levels, recipes, and vouchers for gold so far. I'm probably going to add vouchers for other things that can't be wrapped, too. Maybe even turtle tokens! :O

Q: Well, that all sounds very exciting, but with you being a filthy american, you're never online when I am! And even when you are, your shifts are all over the place! What if I don't see you a particular day?
A: Trust me, I get you. In the case that you can't find Engie in-game, be it because schedules didn't align, or maybe Engie was slacking off that day, you can post a response in this thread, claiming your gift for the day. Engie will mail it to you.

Q: Wait, what's stopping me from just posting in the thread for free stuff?
A: Honestly, nothing. I'd like to see you in-game (roleplay optional), but I cannot force you, and I'm not gonna punish anyone for not being able to be on at the same time as me.

Q: Anything I can do to help?
A: Collecting presents is, admittedly, a *lot* of work. Anything you can donate to the present stash would be appreciated. I'm not expecting anything, and ideally I won't need help, but if you want to donate, I'll make a list of people who have contributed in this post. <3

Either meet with Engie in-game to receive your present (roleplay is encouraged, but not required; just don't be a dick to those who /are/ roleplaying), or post in the thread with your character's name.

Engie will be handing out gifts in the Winter Veil Vale!

Sitting at her desk, the half-goblin stashed her right hand into her pocket and jangled some gold coins. The sound always helped to focus her, but her mind still wandered - it was that time of year again, she supposed. Clink, clink, clink. Chin cupped in her left hand, she tapped her cheek absently. Clink, clink, clink. Tap, tap, tap.

"Arrrrgh!" She suddenly stood up and ran her fingers frantically through her hair. She looked around her office, desperate for something to distract her. "Stupid, wasteful, pointless!" She muttered angrily as she thought again about the upcoming festivities. More specifically, what she wanted to do. Didn't want to do! "No, no, no!" She paced angrily around the room.

Although she prided herself on her goblin heritage, Engie was just as much a gnome, and the jubilant festivities had always enthralled her, whether she liked it or not. And that wouldn't be such a problem - indeed, holidays were a fantastic chance to make some gold! - if not for the fact that every year she was overcome by some stupid urge to give stuff away. For free! There's no profit in giving away your product!

'Everything has a price.' Those words were both the slogan for her company, as well as the words she lived by. Indeed, everything had a price, be it goods, equipment, or services. And to just.... give it away? Uggggh. Her skin crawled at the prospect. And yet, here she was, fighting that exact urge. It was as if she were splitting in two, and each part of herself was warring over what to do.

She screamed in frustration again, then suddenly froze. "Wait. What if I could do both?" She murmured softly. The half-gnome quickly sat back down at her desk and opened a drawer to grab a sheet of paper. The logic was contradictory - to give things away, but to gain a profit in doing so. It was nonsense, but nonsense was often incredibly lucrative. A way to satisfy both her gnomish need for jubilant festivities, and her goblin need for some cash.

She grinned. "Yeah, I can do this."

She set about drawing up a poster for the....


First Annual Engie Industries Advent Exchange

author: Rudi2
subject: Anselm Meyer - Journal Entry 8
content_md:
It has been some months since I have last written in this run-down book about my exploits and journey across the world, both hellish and peaceful landscapes I have witnessed first-hand. I write from Southshore, in which I will explain as to why I am here, and how I traveled. From Darkshore, I have been beseeched by the head Sentinel to proceed along the beaten path to Ashenvale, a region I have heard that has been torn apart by the Legion and the Orcish Horde. During my travels, I have met few adventurers who recognise my face through tabloid and exploits which have transferred from mouth to ear.

It was at this time I came across a great treant who had tasked me to study and return with a book - a book which held scripture of the Old Gods. Not much had come through this task, aside from a small reward which I took graciously and used for supplies to continue my journey.

Ashenvale had few prospects going for it, as many handfuls of adventurers had taken the liberty of assisting the war-torn region with it's issues. In respect, I had given my regards to the Sentinel of the village and shared tobacco with it's male denizens, telling stories of my glory days in the past three wars. Many of which were inspired and in awe of my retelling of the battle which took place at the fabled Dark Portal. Bow and sword in hand as I step-by-step slain the greenskin masses that guarded the very gateway to what we thought was the beginning of Hell. Little to no tangent was sided - many, including the guardswomen who stood outside the inn listened with wide eyes and prideful hearts of the exploits of their Alliance friends. Dwarves, Humans, even High Elves of Quel'thalas standing united against the threat that preceded the current threat that ravaged their homeland.

In surprise, they paid for my room and a meal to fill my stomach for the night. Returning downstairs in the morning, I had taken my leave southeast, toward the direction of Stonetalon Mountains. This would be my first encounter with the Horde-aligned races in many years.
A tauren stood guard between the mountain ranges that divided the aligning regions. Twice as tall as me, with a mace that would rival even the strongest of black steeds that my old army could offer. The Bovine addressed himself as Mahkah. In Tauren tradition, from what I could gather, first names such as that one are given after completion of a feat of strength... which alerted me to some degree. Bow pulled off of my shoulder and arrow in hand, I waited.

In spite of my claims of lack of affiliation, he readied his weapon and waited alongside me, calling me out on what he believed was my bluff. I grew frustrated at his attempts to sway me into pulling my bow back. I called out more and more, claiming in truth of my intentions to simply pass through. A hoof pulled back in a charge, and I took my shot toward his gullet beneath his helmet. Time had felt frozen in that instance. A sin had been committed then and there, attacking without just cause despite self defence. I had struck him with my arrow, hitting his sternum. Just as many deer had fallen to my aim, the bovine goliath had too on his back.
Clutching the arrow with his hand, he could barely breathe. All I remember of that night in terms of dialogue would simply be:

"I'm sorry, Mahkah. I am not ordained in the Light to mend your wounds. I pray for your salvation, however." Sweat had beaded my face in frustration at what he had forced me to do. A hand rested on my shoulder, nearly knocking me to my feet; I remained kneeling as he spoke his last words to me in broken Common. "Spirits guide you, Warrior. Forgive me as I will you in the afterlife."
His words had hit a nerve in me, which I had not felt in some decades. The same situation in repeat, many years to the present.

What I mean by this is a moment in my life that had been on repeat in my mind for some days after the run-in with Mahkah. During the last days of my service to the Light, I had been sent on patrol through what is now known as the Western Plaguelands in Lordaeron. The Dawn had encountered many of our patrols to and from Tyr's Hand, where I was stationed. Arrows shot from all directions toward our sentries before an ambush of fighters came from the brushes to meet our crusaders. A woman, I had been dueling separate from the group, wore the tabard of the Dawn, just as I had the Crusade. Claiming I had deserted, she took me on one-versus-one. Sixteen bouts in, we had nary a dent in eachothers armour let alone blood which little had been spilled. I held two blades while she had a sword and shield. A fine display in the way of the sword which we both admired for a solid minute, exchanging words of gratitude toward one another. Before I knew it, a bullet had shot in my side by ricochet through the back of my hip, barreling toward the woman I had been dueling.
The bullet had hit her chest in the same place that the tauren had been killed. She fell to her front, kneeling over panting in an attempt to recover from her wound. We both were simply fighters, trained in the art of the blade rather than the Light. She was a goliath, in spirit. She was in the range of being saved, however. Helping her to her feet as blood trailed our path, I dragged her away from the battlefield, toward her camp which patrols scoured, watching me in disbelief as I carried the plated woman to her brethren. They received her well, and ran in all directions to gather supplies and the holyman to heal her. How I left that camp alive - is up to the reader to decide.

In any case, I buried my enemy, covering his grave in reeds and limbs from trees to decompose just as he would.
For those wondering as to why I write and publish these articles, there is no reason. Life goes on as souls are taken and life is given. I am destitute and alone in my journey to find purpose and salvation for crimes and sin that has gone unpunished and unforgiven in the eyes of the Church. I am no cleric, nor a paladin to cast judgement for the blood I've drawn from my enemies and the lives I've ruined in war... Until I reached Stormwind, where my journey had originally began.

To pay tithe and pray for the life I had slain, a boy approached me by the name of Thomas who sought my presence for a task.
"Anselm, Sir? It's been some months since you have been to service. Are you okay?" The boy tugged at my tattered armour to get my attention, which I had replied.
"Yes, I am. I've just returned from Kalimdor, taking in odd jobs so I may donate my spoils and pay my dues. What seems the matter?"
The boy pointed to a peculiar corner in the Cathedral, which was dark and considerably more less kept than the rest of the building combined. "Brother Crowley needs you."

That name sent a shiver down my spine and splinters through my bones. With a lit torch I descended down the staircase which the boy guided me down to a small crypt-like room with red tapestry and brazen torches and candlelight. A man in crimson robes and friar hat came from behind a pillar. He wore a tabard of the Scarlet Crusade, just as I had many years ago. "Your crime for treason had not gone unnoticed, Brother Anselm." A finger came out from the sleeve of his robe, with gloves that had the fingers cut out from them. Thomas had already been up the stairs by the time Brother Crowley had revealed himself. "Take your penance and let me speak with you, for I have a task to bestow upon you." To which I agreed, and penance was taken at the hand of Brother Crowley. After a brief rest, I was allowed back on my feet. Exchanging words, it was decided that I return to the scene of my now-realised crimes, to Tirisfal Glades where I go on my path now, resting at Southshore.

author: Rudi2
subject: Anselm Meyer - Journal Entry 8
content_md:
Some days have passed as I continued my journey to the Glades of Lordaeron. Beautiful landscapes from trekking through the Wetlands, to Arathi; my old home. It had been some time since I had set foot in the Highlands, from arid mountains to it's flat plains. Raptors, elementals, the odd coyote. I let out an audible breath of fresh air the moment I took a step over the Thandol Span that divided the seas and connected Arathor and Lordaeron to Azeroth.

In that moment, I thought a good moment while walking the trail across my homeland. I knelt down a ways from the path and took in a handful of dirt, letting it sift into the leather folds of my gloves. This is the earth we inhabit yet destruction for hundreds, thousands, even a millions of lives that had been lost both inhuman: the Elves, Tauren, Orcs, and the Human: our kind, the Dwarves, and the Gnomes is still widespread. I alone cannot prevent lives being lost as the land I've walked across is barren of life, as citizens hide and adventurers do in their own time what they can to help.

I carried on until I hit the bridge to Stromgarde. The castle-city I had frequently traveled to in my childhood that was some leagues away from my manor house was grey, and dull. As if the paint off of roofs of buildings and the colour of it's stone walls and cobblestone paths had been taken in a vacuum by a malefic being. A sight to behold in my seniority, as I have not set eyes on this castle-city since my youth. Every bone in my body felt magnetised toward the condensed mass of marble and stone, seduced by nostalgia. I had to look away, as tears filled my ducts and filmed over my eyes. I had to walk away, and continue on to my quest.

So we meet to present day in Southshore, where I write this passage and the one before it. I will admit, the scars of penance that Brother Crowley had bestowed upon me on my back are still sore, and my feet ache crossing multiple terrains. On the bright side, it had been six weeks since my last alcoholic beverage, seeing as how water is in surplus whether it be from lakes or waterfalls. If I had a mind, I'd say this is a sign of improvement. I wish to keep this trend going for the coming days of meeting my contact in the Glades to speak terms of my redemption for desertion.

The briefing of my task was simple. Report to a Crusader who was resting at Soliden Farm, one of the many settlements that have not fallen to the Forsaken Scourge as of yet and he will give me the details of my redemption. I am to give him a letter of commendation and absolution of sin which Brother Crowley had written prior to us meeting.

So we meet to present day in Southshore, where I write this passage and the one before it. I will admit, the scars of penance that Brother Crowley had bestowed upon me on my back are still sore, and my feet ache crossing multiple terrains. On the bright side, it had been six weeks since my last alcoholic beverage, seeing as how water is in surplus whether it be from lakes or waterfalls. If I had a mind, I'd say this is a sign of improvement. I wish to keep this trend going for the coming days of meeting my contact in the Glades to speak terms of my redemption for desertion.

The briefing of my task was simple. Report to a Crusader who was resting at Soliden Farm, one of the many settlements that have not fallen to the Forsaken Scourge as of yet and he will give me the details of my redemption. I am to give him a letter of commendation and absolution of sin which Brother Crowley had written prior to us meeting.

author: Kazgrim
subject: For Honor
content_md:
Kazog lowered his hood as he entered the dimly lit inn, moving towards his usual spot. He sat down and gestured towards the patron for a drink. Not soon after a cup of grog was placed in front of him, of which he soon downed with no time to spare. The glaring Barrens sun had worn down on him, and it had been a few days since his journey that he had something to drink. There had been some hiccups in his travels that he had not anticipated, which Kazog could now ponder upon and bury.

Thunder clashed as clouds gathered far over the horizon. A storm was brewing, and so Kazog sought shelter from the lightning. The amber landscape soon became grey with shadow as the tempest grew near, the thunderbolts roaring like the stampede of a kodo herd. As Kazog searched for a place to hide, he saw ahead of him an abandoned orc burrow. He entered the wreckage that was once someone's home, crouching in the corner where the ceiling had not caved in. It was dark, and debris laid everywhere. It was wet too, but Kazog could not see what from. As he sat there contemplating the journey ahead, he reached for his water flask, prepared to take a sip. As his lips touched the flask he heard a soft voice that began to fill the tiny room. Startled, Kazog stood to his feet, grasping at the hilt of his axe as he searched for where the whispers came from. He took a step forward as the voice grew nearer, and looked down at a pile of dust and rubble. Between the void space of that debris he saw a hand reaching out to him, its tiny fingers clawing at air. Eyes stared back at Kazog, shining beneath the shadows. Kazog hesitated before throwing away the rubble ontop of the child, clearing the debris that had somehow not crushed the infant. He stood there, looking down in disbelief. The child playfully snorted and huffed air, looking up at Kazog with bewildered eyes. It gestured towards Kazog's flask, which Kazog gripped against his chest. Kazog knelt down and lowered the flask to the child's snout, watching in apprehension as the child thirstly consumed all that was left.

Kazog sighed. He knew that the child would not remember him, or what he had done. He knew that it would one day grow from a child into a warrior, and become his enemy. Kazog knew what he had to do.

Kazog left the burrow, leaving behind his hesitations and second thoughts. He turned from the direction he had headed and now treaded in his own footsteps. The soft murmurs of a child carried on his back was all that needed to remind him of where he was now headed. In the distance great thorns rose from the plains, enveloping a place in shadow darker than those tempest born.

Kazog crouched hidden in tall blades of grass, waiting for the patrol to turn its back. As the guardsmen disappeared from view, Kazog left the cover of the savannah and approached the campfire. Night had fallen, and the tribe stirred silently in their sleep. Kazog reached over his shoulder to gently place the child from his back onto the ground by the fire. He wrapped the blanket tightly over the infant, saying his goodbyes. He stared down at the child, looking into its eyes, hoping it would one day remember. He then darted back towards the safety of the grass, not before turning to look for one last time. As he hesitated, the piercing sound of an arrow cut through the air and plunged into Kazog's shoulder. Kazog turned from the force of the blow, blood dripping down his arm. He sprinted towards the direction he had came, away from the sound of shouts and snarls that now stalked him in the night.

Kazog placed a hand on his shoulder, but soon dropped it to the table. There was nothing to be said, no words to explain. He took another swig of grog and fell asleep, waking up the next day only to have forgotten.

author: Rudi2
subject: The Eagles and the Vultures
content_md:
"Time heals all wounds."

Noon at the Scarlet Raven, in Darkshire. The region is known for the scourged undead which roam it's countryside. Worgen, wild hounds and spiders that harm the public which dare to venture to friendlier towns. Years of inactivity and shirking the responsibilities of my superiors, lying low had made me anxious. The fervor that had settled after my transgressions in the past had finally regained it's kindle. Now to do something about it.

(Outside of the book,) Just moments after I had written that, I went ahead and shut my tome and put it in my satchel, downing my last few drops of lager, I looked up to the bartender and said thus:

"So the Kingdom pays little attention to your town's needs. Why stand idle behind your business with hope that the idle adventurer like me pays attention for a reward?"
The bartender of the shift stared, and stared in silence at the truth that, even an outsider, knows of the ailment that plights the now-known Duskwood. "What of it, stranger? Help here from your kind demand a reward."
"A reward is without the security of knowing the task is complete to the end. The ends justify the means, knave." I slid my empty mug to the gentleman and stood up from my seat, turning to the few citizens that sat in despair, dwelling with their thoughs.

 **"BROTHERS AND SISTERS!"** *Without exaggeration my voice cracked and boomed through the decrepit wood walls and ceiling of the tavern, eyes turning to me in a flash. Hoarse and explosive to the ear, though without the desire to cover their ears.* **"I HAVE SEEN ENOUGH! YOUR KING RESTS LAZILY AND YOUR TOWN IN DISREPAIR! I HAVE SAT DOWN IN MANY BARS LOOKING BACK AT WHAT COULD HAVE BEEN WITH MY LIFE, WHAT SAY YOU TO THE FUTURE OF YOUR PEOPLE!?"** *Of course a speech does kill my voice somewhat, the louder and longer I screamed the truth, some grew disruptive, others began to appear riled up and restless - even annoyed at the naysayers which later would turn to consider violence.*
 **"SHUT UP WILL YOU?" A man at the corner of the bar would say, then a woman from another side. "SOD OFF, OUTSIDER!"** Those willing to listen finally snapped, as chairs flew across the room. The entire tavern split in two the moment the first fist flew. I stood in disbelief for a time, as my voice that filled the room would be replaced with the noise of riot. This would not be the guard's concern, seeing some members of the Night's Watch stand at the entrance of the tavern, arms crossed to see how this would go. As noble as their cause was to defend the town, it seems to me that politics of the Kingdom caused some debate more than needed.
Finally, a burly man which seemed around my age charged up the bar's steps with a shattered glass bottle, arm out ready to jab at my shoulder. With a lunge of my foot toward a nearby a barstool, I kicked the stool up to my level, catching it with both hands.
I had sent the stool flying toward the aggressor's hand which bore the knife, smacking into his fist with full force. The man clutched his knuckles, screaming at the sudden impact of teak wood and screws. While to me it seemed as if it was pure luck that I would strike with such accuracy. He knew to back away into the rabble of dissent. The town guard came to, pulling away those that had fallen unconscious and wounded in the barfight, even arresting those who refused to cease. Those left standing, which appeared to be the majority of who had agreed with my ravings, stood in silence at my call.

"You are all pious and noble to defend the truth that even a traveler would know, that the King does not care. The nobles in the castle are just as dishonest and tyrannous as the bandits that decided to be of the collective to take arms. Those guards just outside, listening."
I pointed out to the corridor which lead to the exit of the tavern. My voice had gone to a hush, leaning into the small crowd.
"They do their job, but even they know that the foundation your town rests on a lie that hope is on their side, that the King will send help. But He falls silent."

 *We will be that help.*

content_md:
Skorgrim looked over the rag-tag group of conscripts, letting out a sigh of frustration. "I suppose this will do." He looked each man in the eye, testing to see if their nerve would be enough for the horrors that led ahead. "Alright, move out!"

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738781189275679/WoWScrnShot_040320_152314.jpg)

Skorgrim and his caravan moved through the forests of Elwynn and Duskwood, putting to death bandit and beast that obstructed their way. Just as they prepared to enter the dreaded Deadwind Pass, a foul wind blew past Skorgrim and his warriors. "Brace yourselves, lads. Dark magic flows freely, corrupting this wretched land." He threw his cloak over his head, walking up the shadowy path towards the ominous ivory tower in the distance. As he and his group approached a large ravine, a cloaked figure stood guard with several others He greeted them, and they made their way together down towards the lowlands. "These orcs will guide us to our destination, try not to cause any trouble."

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738781948706846/WoWScrnShot_040320_153545.jpg)

The group made their way to the forgotten tomb. They parked themselves outside the entrance as Skorgrim gathered his explosives. "STAND BACK!" He yelled, as a large bang went off. The iron gate that sealed the tomb blew off its handles, clearing the pathway inside. "Orcs first."

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738784611958836/WoWScrnShot_040320_155043.jpg)

Skorgrim turned to Kazgrim. "A deal's a deal." Said the annoyed Dwarf, out-stretching his hand for payment. Skorgrim stood at the edge of a tunnel that led into a dark abyss with no end in sight. Kazgrim snorted before pushing Skorgrim backwards, his body disappearing into the darkness. "If the rest of you wish to not meet a similar fate, then follow me." He motioned for the others to follow him deeper into the catacombs.

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738786566504478/WoWScrnShot_040320_160538.jpg)

It became apparent that there was no great treasure to be found in this wretched place, only death. As Kazgrim led the group deeper into the crypt, they arrived in a room littered with skulls and bones. At the center of the room was an altar, which Kazgrim stood behind. He motioned for the others to come closer. The group approached the altar, save for the paladin that now held his sword in hand, ready to slay Kazgrim. "Place your hand on this altar, and I shall reward you immensely."

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738789011914812/WoWScrnShot_040320_161125.jpg)

One by one the members of the group placed their hand on the altar, their soul now bound to Kazgrim's dark ritual. A mirror into a dark abyss appeared before them all, and a demon exited from it. It stood higher than them all, its head scraping the ceiling of the catacombs. With one fell swipe of its blade, it severed the body of one of its summoners in half. Kazgrim broke into a terrible laughter. "Kill them all!"

![Image](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/556152826502447129/695738790651756636/WoWScrnShot_040320_161150.jpg)

The paladin that stood behind now rushed forward, gripping his sword with a zealous fervor. He and the others fought to slay the terrible beast, sacrificing many wounds in order to do so. When the beast finally fell, they laid exhausted from the long fight, barely able to hold themselves up. Kazgrim, dismayed that his plan did not come to fruition, snarled in anger. He began to cast a spell to destroy them all when Aurrius, the paladin that had stepped forward to save them all, charged Kazgrim, attempting to disrupt his spell. What followed was a fierce duel between the two. Aurrius' strength, however, had waned considerably, and Kazgrim was able to stun him long enough to summon a portal for escape. In the end, Kazgrim fled unscathed, although his plans were foiled. He would need to look elsewhere if he were to summon a great power to wield for his own.

A letter is delivered to you by an exhausted dwarf mountaineer, he cant give you any explanation until he recovers his breath, meanwhile, he just encourages you to read the letter. It is sealed with a simple wax, yet you can distinguish the wildhammer dwarf sigil on it.

Feel free to accept this invitation if ya have the liver enought to make it throught ta night, and ta patience enought to endure some old bad jokes. Ta meetin is goin to be at ol´ Kharanos, two moons after ya get this letter. Make sure to bring some good Ale, ´Cuz Im not goin to buy ya ale all ta night, ya lazzy a..... (The ink is a little blurred here).... And make sure you get yar manners to."

> Defenders of Azeroth,
>

author: Jam
subject: Rekgor's Travels
content_md:
((There is a self imposed challenge suggested on the forums, linked below, that I made this toon for. Originally part of my warrior's backstory, I didn't have much plan for Rekgor but now I'm putting a little bit of time into him sporadically and I'll add forum posts recapping his travels.))

[viewtopic.php?p=6459#p6459](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=6459#p6459)

"The shaman's old callused hand gripped the wood handle of his issued mace. He dug his toes into the coarse rocks and sand outside The Den. He had submitted himself to retraining as a shaman. The elements of this world recognized him, he knew. They had saved his life in the mines of the barrens more than once but they would not answer when he called. So here he stood, among orcs a third his age and trolls learning the shamanistic ways. Being sent to kill boar as a test of his skill. He jogged off into the valley until he saw his first target. He reached up to beseech the elements for power and smile came to his grizzled face as he felt the energy crackling around his outstretched hand. He focused on the boar and thrust his arm forward, sending the lightning hurtling through the dry air."

"There was a time in this orcs long life when the lightning that flowed through him would incapacitate the wild beasts of his home world. He reflected on those times as the lightning pounded into the boar and the beast, barely phased, charged towards him in anger. The orc met the charge, a tusk digging deep into his leg as he brought the mace down and ended the boars life with a savage blow. Pain seared through his leg as he felt the dampness of blood roll down and into his ankle wraps. He felt something else. He felt alive. He called upon the elements to heal his wound and they did. He looked at the mace and with a smirk stuffed it into his bag. He would survive by the elements or he would die."

"With renewed vigor and a sense of purpose he'd not felt in years, the orc carried on. He killed the boar necessary, taking meat, hides and tusks back to The Den. He gathered cactus fruit for Galgar, helped a troll that had fallen to a large black scorpid, and cleared a den of demons that had gathered around a corrupt warlock." Rekgor leaned back against the wall in the Razor Hill inn, "Now young ones, my story is at a break." He tapped the ash out of his pipe against the wall before carefully tucking it into his pack. "After I've rested a bit I set out to Sen'jin to help the trolls there, and to see what help I can render and to see what the elements of Azeroth have still to teach me."

Rekgor smiled as the small crowd dispersed. His body ached now and his movements were wrought with stiffness and pain. Days swinging a pick and tossing rocks were nothing compared to running and fighting. Sleep came to him easily, swinging in the rope hammock. He dreamed of his younger days, prior to drinking the demon blood. The atrocities he committed while under the influence of that foul substance could not be forgotten but for the first night in years they were a side note to his slumber and not the focal point.

author: Illyane
subject: [no-RP] How vivid is the RP ('n community) there ?
content_md:
Hello there fellow Roleplayers,

Coming from the dying french RP communities where I've played (and mostly doing the exhausting grunt job of being a GM-creator) the past 15 years, I'm currently searching an active RP server. I have currently obtained much informations about the events, contents, and how the RP is supposed to be played on this little turtle (by chatting in the game, visiting the discord and reading the forum), but I had the feeling that the ambiance wasn't really "RP".

Even if I can be characterized as a hardcore Roleplayer, I'm not the type to request that from everybody else (I'm not against non-rp chat, casual speak and other thing that can trigger roleplayers), but I thought that there will be some "infrastructures" to welcome roleplayers here. From what I've investigated : there is no RP plugin given with the ZIP of the Game (like pre-installed add-ons, ig RP tutorial, etc.), there is no way to present ourself and to meet instantly after creating our char the community by joining a "world" for the Roleplayers (for organizing events, etc.). I've seen absolutely no events or active community projects being displayed (RP cities? community structures?). To be brief, there is nothing here facilitating the creation of any kind of RP community alchemy (For what I've seen so far, I beg you to change my mind).

The answers I got were pretty casual. Kind people (I mean it, I met patient and really nice people gently answering my queries without grumble, pretty rare and I must say it), kind people tell me that meeting on the street Roleplayers is not really common, and that most of the guilds are doing their stuff in their corners.

So, how is it? How vivid is the RP community here? Is there anything that can evoke "Vanilla" in the RP experience (like the good old days)? How would you describe your experience of roleplay here? Am I missing a point in your opinion? Is there official projects that are being worked on to facilitate RP ig ? And so, should I try to pexx a char to 60?

I thank you for the lecture of this... This. And I'm waiting your answers :)
Best regards, Illyane

content_md:
There is nothing additive to the download as the Turtles, in their wisdom, wanted people to be able to get their own download, rather than have to host it themselves and open themselves up for legal liability.

That being said, there are several recommended add-ons and tweaks linked to in these forums. If you are an RPer, I would suggest your first step is to get MyRP, which flags you as an RPer to other RPers. There is a working link in the addons section of the forums.

While it is true that open RP isn't super common, it does happen, you just have to be in the right place. You are correct, though, in that mostof it goes on inside of guilds. Guilds sometimes have Guild Houses, structures built inside of the game to represent the guild hall of a guild. I know of two off-hand. One in Darkshire and one in Deadwind Pass, but I know there is more. The Admins do not create these willy-nilly, but only for guilds who stick around a while and have RP ideas on why they should warrant a bunch of work on the GM's part.

Being a player from the BC era, I do not find the tons of RP in the Stormwind Park I found pre-cataclysm (or Blue Recluse Post-cata), but the population here is nowhere near that of a live server. IMO, it is what you make of it.

author: Illyane
subject: Re: [no-RP] How vivid is the RP ('n community) there ?
content_md:
It is less about things I would like to see happening than means left at the disposition of roleplayers. The main problem with an RP community is that it literally drains time from any game master, staff member or server administrator who would want administrate it or organise events. It's fine to organise things, but you can't be everywhere, you can't watch everything, and you can't organise everything. So you need to put on place tools to facilitate the RP without obliterate your free time, or destroying the balance of the server (like how god mod or spawning artefacts can without control). That's where you need to consider the infrastructure that can offer the server. Literally, if you put a road and the signalization, everybody will use it without much question.

What I mean by that is that the server offer many possibilities to facilitate the process of formation of an active RP community. Actually, the community is already active for what I can observe (it seems that there are dozens of RP players here, that already a large community by my standards, well for a BFA standard that's it), but for newcomers and newbies, the integration can only be slow and perhaps annoying. (I need to install Add-on, I need to find by luck a canal, try again my luck to find an active roleplayer, I don't know who is a roleplayer or not, I don't know in game if there are any event currently in place, I need to make long researches, I need to...).

For an RP community to be more dynamic, we need in my opinion mainly five points : (1) First is to offer a clear choice to anybody to become a roleplayer, (2) Second is to know who is an ACTIVE roleplayer, (3) Third is to rend easy the contact between roleplayers, and between creators and roleplayers, (4) Fourth is to facilitate the advertising of community events and deeds, (5) Fifth is to increase the global "immersion". This server offer game mechanics that can have their use in the dynamization of an RP community.

 **I. Example : The magnificent Glyph system.**
When we create a character here, we receive a gentle turtle that propose us in-game shop as well as a hardcore levelling glyph. This amazing glyph system can propose RP modifiers too:

To answer (1), (2) and partially (3) and (4) : Communication, finding and meeting.
Instead of forcing people to install add-on and to literally "work" to be able to just create an only RP profile, how about a glyph that activate pre-installed (visible, but non-active) Add-on (my rp and stuff) ? The player who choose to take the glyph from Turtle will be recognize as an RP player for a register (It is possible to see on the website how many players are actually connected, you can show with that how many roleplayers are currently ingame), and will join two canals, one OORP to meet the community, another one RP where announcements and advertisings can be done by creators who want to make aware other of rumours, recruitment campaigns, RP quest, Tavern and other casual events (there is nothing like that for now).  This glyph can actually help to reference an "annular" page on the website (like : active roleplayers).

To answer (3) : Meeting, guilds and events :
[1] A "RP Guild master Glyph", where an RP player can form a guild, and automatically be referenced as an active guild master for an RP project. Any person who would like to search for an RP guild would just have to see a webpage of Turtle to see all of the projects referenced (like he should be able to see how many roleplayer there is on the server). When a guy choose this glyph, he is invited to create a presentation topic of his guild on the forum.
[2] A "RP meeting Glyph", who permits any roleplayer to join with a special hearthstone an RP tavern (like a dimensional one open by a strange magus). Anybody who just want to RP without putting to much on it will just have to use it to meet the others. Et voilà, you don't have to organize yourself everyday events, just have a horde and alliance vendors of drinks and foods (and even the possibility for anybody to obtain a "glyph of staff" to work here as a server or a bartender).

To answer (5) : Immersion :
Our chance is that Vanilla is already pretty immersive. The mobs are violent, the quests simple, in fact, the PVE/PVP system is pretty brutal. The need resides again in the "graphic" immersion, and the possibility to make you hero "more human".
[1] A "Glyph of RP immersion", that activate another pre-installed Add-on (but non-activated), Darker nights, and if possible a thing that make look the weather events more "huge". Like when there is a tempest in Stranglethorn, the rain must be strong as f*ck (for the last one, about weather, I think it will be more difficult).
[2] A "Glyph of effort", that limit by example running in city spaces (the ideal should be everywhere, but that's asking to much). Running could be a competences for roleplayers scaled on stamina (the more you have stamina, the longer you can run).

Etc. It's possible to make even a "Total RP" glyph, a hardcore RP levelling mod that change the way the player is supposed to play. (He can't run all he wants, He need to sleep on a bed in the tavern/tent to be rested, he needs to eats every 4 hours -hence malus-, to drink every hours, he needs to tend his wounds if his hp are less than 10%) and all that was show before. A way of making the game and pexxing even slower, but that give "recompenses" like the hardcore way of levelling do.

With the glyph system that's already in place and so less complicated I guess to modify, you can increase any the dynamic around an RP community, letting the choice without forcing the hand (like the hardcore levelling system doesn't make the hardcore leveller "better" or anything in comparison with another, the "hardcore RP player" will just be a type of roleplayer that will find a gameplay up to his tastes). You can like that generate a type of RP that is similar to the one we can see on any other blizzard server, to be safely away from the trap that are private RP-GM servers, but still offering more tools that can complete the offer turtle is trying to put in place. This is just an example, one that can increase the attractiveness of this server as an RP hub, without to much disturbing the PVE and asking to much time monitoring it. I didn't approach the skin shop and stuff because that's more about tastes and visions than community dynamic.

 **II. Other examples :**

Other things are about communication : In my opinion, we miss a thing between the main website and the forum. There should be more specific pages, one who presents the server and his features, one about the quality of the PVE system, one about the RP (how he is played, what are the tricks to know… etc.) and not just links to forum threads. But that’s purely marketing and communication grumbles on my part. I’ve found a little bit long to search everything on the forum, discord and in-game just to be able to understand how is supposed to work the RP here.

Last point is about Charters : Everybody seems nice here, so it didn’t seem immediately a necessity, but the more this cool server will be known, the more we will need a charter from turtle to protect the immersion, the ambiance. Like, If you aren’t a Roleplayer, breaking the immersion of them is punishable (for an example).

That’s what I mean by “infrastructure”, basic in-game structures that need work to be put in place, but that reduce  the workload after. If you have this type of things in place, you will have less worries about a need to “offer” events to the community because if tools like the ones aforementioned before were implemented, if the community die, it will be only her own fault. After that, everything will be a bonus, a kind a happy gift for the community by the staff. The apparition of a giant nerubian in the eastern plagueland ? Just a narrative text presenting the threat on the website *(five lines : "[...] The evil hidden in Naxxramas has unleashed a new threat against the mortal [...]")*, an immersive announcement in-game (a town crier?), et voilà, it’s in the lore that there is a giant nerubian.  :)

I hope what I’ve written is understandable ^^’ If you doesn’t understand anything, please tell me, I will rewrite it   smiling_turtle

It's fine to organise things, but you can't be everywhere, you can't watch everything, and you can't organise everything. So you need to put on place tools to facilitate the RP without obliterate your free time, or destroying the balance of the server (like how god mod or spawning artefacts can without control). That's where you need to consider the infrastructure that can offer the server. Literally, if you put a road and the signalization, everybody will use it without much question.

What I mean by that is that the server offer many possibilities to facilitate the process of formation of an active RP community. Actually, the community is already active for what I can observe (it seems that there are dozens of RP players here, that already a large community by my standards, well for a BFA standard that's it), but for newcomers and newbies, the integration can only be slow and perhaps annoying. (I need to install Add-on, I need to find by luck a canal, try again my luck to find an active roleplayer, I don't know who is a roleplayer or not, I don't know in game if there are any event currently in place, I need to make long researches, I need to...).

For an RP community to be more dynamic, we need in my opinion mainly five points : (1) First is to offer a clear choice to anybody to become a roleplayer, (2) Second is to know who is an ACTIVE roleplayer, (3) Third is to rend easy the contact between roleplayers, and between creators and roleplayers, (4) Fourth is to facilitate the advertising of community events and deeds, (5) Fifth is to increase the global "immersion". This server offer game mechanics that can have their use in the dynamization of an RP community.

I. Example : The magnificent Glyph system.
When we create a character here, we receive a gentle turtle that propose us in-game shop as well as a hardcore levelling glyph. This amazing glyph system can propose RP modifiers too:

To answer (1), (2) and partially (3) and (4) : Communication, finding and meeting.
Instead of forcing people to install add-on and to literally "work" to be able to just create an only RP profile, how about a glyph that activate pre-installed (visible, but non-active) Add-on (my rp and stuff) ? The player who choose to take the glyph from Turtle will be recognize as an RP player for a register (It is possible to see on the website how many players are actually connected, you can show with that how many roleplayers are currently ingame), and will join two canals, one OORP to meet the community, another one RP where announcements and advertisings can be done by creators who want to make aware other of rumours, recruitment campaigns, RP quest, Tavern and other casual events (there is nothing like that for now). This glyph can actually help to reference an "annular" page on the website (like : active roleplayers).

To answer (3) : Meeting, guilds and events :
[1] A "RP Guild master Glyph", where an RP player can form a guild, and automatically be referenced as an active guild master for an RP project. Any person who would like to search for an RP guild would just have to see a webpage of Turtle to see all of the projects referenced (like he should be able to see how many roleplayer there is on the server). When a guy choose this glyph, he is invited to create a presentation topic of his guild on the forum.
[2] A "RP meeting Glyph", who permits any roleplayer to join with a special hearthstone an RP tavern (like a dimensional one open by a strange magus). Anybody who just want to RP without putting to much on it will just have to use it to meet the others. Et voilà, you don't have to organize yourself everyday events, just have a horde and alliance vendors of drinks and foods (and even the possibility for anybody to obtain a "glyph of staff" to work here as a server or a bartender).

To answer (5) : Immersion :
Our chance is that Vanilla is already pretty immersive. The mobs are violent, the quests simple, in fact, the PVE/PVP system is pretty brutal. The need resides again in the "graphic" immersion, and the possibility to make you hero "more human".
[1] A "Glyph of RP immersion", that activate another pre-installed Add-on (but non-activated), Darker nights, and if possible a thing that make look the weather events more "huge". Like when there is a tempest in Stranglethorn, the rain must be strong as f*ck (for the last one, about weather, I think it will be more difficult).
[2] A "Glyph of effort", that limit by example running in city spaces (the ideal should be everywhere, but that's asking to much). Running could be a competences for roleplayers scaled on stamina (the more you have stamina, the longer you can run).

Etc. It's possible to make even a "Total RP" glyph, a hardcore RP levelling mod that change the way the player is supposed to play. (He can't run all he wants, He need to sleep on a bed in the tavern/tent to be rested, he needs to eats every 4 hours -hence malus-, to drink every hours, he needs to tend his wounds if his hp are less than 10%) and all that was show before. A way of making the game and pexxing even slower, but that give "recompenses" like the hardcore way of levelling do.

With the glyph system that's already in place and so less complicated I guess to modify, you can increase any the dynamic around an RP community, letting the choice without forcing the hand (like the hardcore levelling system doesn't make the hardcore leveller "better" or anything in comparison with another, the "hardcore RP player" will just be a type of roleplayer that will find a gameplay up to his tastes). You can like that generate a type of RP that is similar to the one we can see on any other blizzard server, to be safely away from the trap that are private RP-GM servers, but still offering more tools that can complete the offer turtle is trying to put in place. This is just an example, one that can increase the attractiveness of this server as an RP hub, without to much disturbing the PVE and asking to much time monitoring it. I didn't approach the skin shop and stuff because that's more about tastes and visions than community dynamic.

II. Other examples :

Other things are about communication : In my opinion, we miss a thing between the main website and the forum. There should be more specific pages, one who presents the server and his features, one about the quality of the PVE system, one about the RP (how he is played, what are the tricks to know… etc.) and not just links to forum threads. But that’s purely marketing and communication grumbles on my part. I’ve found a little bit long to search everything on the forum, discord and in-game just to be able to understand how is supposed to work the RP here.

Last point is about Charters : Everybody seems nice here, so it didn’t seem immediately a necessity, but the more this cool server will be known, the more we will need a charter from turtle to protect the immersion, the ambiance. Like, If you aren’t a Roleplayer, breaking the immersion of them is punishable (for an example).

That’s what I mean by “infrastructure”, basic in-game structures that need work to be put in place, but that reduce the workload after. If you have this type of things in place, you will have less worries about a need to “offer” events to the community because if tools like the ones aforementioned before were implemented, if the community die, it will be only her own fault. After that, everything will be a bonus, a kind a happy gift for the community by the staff. The apparition of a giant nerubian in the eastern plagueland ? Just a narrative text presenting the threat on the website (five lines : "[...] The evil hidden in Naxxramas has unleashed a new threat against the mortal [...]"), an immersive announcement in-game (a town crier?), et voilà, it’s in the lore that there is a giant nerubian. :)

I hope what I’ve written is understandable ^^’ If you doesn’t understand anything, please tell me, I will rewrite it

content_md:
i can attempt to adress a point or two as I understand them. I'm sorry for picking apart a bit of this, and I sympathize with English not being your native language, but you seem to be making more than one point per heading and I'm trying to understand through the language barrier.

> The player who choose to take the glyph from Turtle will be recognize as an RP player for a register

Would you like something like from the old Everquest days? EQ had a command, /rp, that changed your character's name to blue, I think it was, then other people could immediately see you were a roleplayer as everyone else's name was green. Furthermore when you changed your flag you could search for /rp on your /who command to see other roleplayers. This had a side benefit of hiding your level as you shouldn't be able to see how strong someone is by mousing over them (RP-wise, just looking at them). There was also a /ooc flag, which did much the same, just a different color name tag.

Also, would a world RP channel help out with this?  Like the world chat we already enjoy, just one specifically for RP.

> Instead of forcing people to install add-on and to literally "work" to be able to just create an only RP profile, how about a glyph that activate pre-installed (visible, but non-active) Add-on (my rp and stuff)

So far, nothing is added to the client. That will eventually change, so the "work" is on us. This will change in the future as the Turtles are planning an expac.
I'd love to see an in-game toggle panel for this kind of thing, rather than the somewhat clunky glyph system we already have, but I believe that is a limitation of the client. Glyphs are a decent work-around, but they ARE a work-around.
There have been some player-made quests that have been added to the game to make certain options more understandable. I'd like to see the available options expanded upon through mini-quests at starting zones, but I utterly fail at making quests myself.

> RP where announcements and advertisings can be done by creators who want to make aware other of rumours

There are RP subforums here, but without there being an in-game web browser, it is unlikely that other players will actually consistently use a web page as I think you mean.
A friend of mine once told me, after I told him of the extensive tutorials I wrote for the guild I was currently in, "Man, I don't do any of that, I just wanna play." I have come to understand that this mindset of the norm, regardless how helpful outside information is. i.e. You can't expect or force others to use outside-of-game resources. An in-game web browser is immersion breaking and a limit of the client, I'm sure.

> "RP Guild master Glyph"

I believe that was addressed above.

> "RP meeting Glyph"

This is what the Portable Wormhole Generator is for. It was previously a Portable Meeting stone, that was given to players at character creation, but that was removed in favor of the current PWG becaue of abuse, I believe.

> "Glyph of RP immersion"

I understand this as wanting weather effects to have in-game effects, which I am for, but I cannot see how such a big  systems change that would affect only people with the glyph. I am not a programmer, though, just a guy who collects information.

> "Glyph of effort"

This has been discussed before, but the idea petered out. I really don't know what became of it, other than folks setting their personal "challenges" to walk only in their own "Ultra-Hardcore Mega Mode", which isn't a toggle in-game, just a personal preference. (and thereby no one knowing if they cheated their own goal)

The rest of your post I think was answered above, except for the ending,

> The apparition of a giant nerubian in the eastern plagueland ? Just a narrative text presenting the threat on the website

Which I understand to be GM events. The Sands of Time forums somewhat addresses this with game additive announcements.

Also, as I know it, the GM staff is pretty small. I do not fault them for what they can accomplish in a day. They have to tend wounds and stuck characters and I have seen with my own eyes them build from nothing Guild Bases for RP purposes, complete with an Innkeeper so guildies can hearth back to their guildbase at any time along with vendors and NPCs to facilitate the RP there. If they don't get the chance to insert an event where a sudden plague of rats spreads throughout westfall, I know it is because of lack of manpower, rather than lack of want.

I do not intend this post to belittle yours. I am not employed by the Turtles and I do not know everything. I just try to help. If I missed points, please correct me.

content_md: RP is pretty hands off by the devs. Players are left to initiate it. I personally enjoy being able to level my character and RP at the same time. Turtle WoW embodies that. It’s not a pure RP server with gm commands, etc. Expectations for RP when it comes to Turtle WoW are as follows: Don’t expect random RP interactions (most people are here to pve), Lookout for events, as this is the bread and butter of RP here. As someone who has hosted multiple events, This is my experience when it comes to RP on Turtle WoW. Also, the level of RP here is far less serious than on other servers. People take it very laxxed. Even during RP, dont expect full immersion. You would need to find a group of hardcore RPers, the majority of players here who casually RP don’t take it 100% seriously. That being said, as someone who has come from pure RP servers, its a nice change. I prefer the casualness of it all.

subject: Would it be alright to Roleplay as a Dragon?
content_md:
Hi there, passing through to toss this question to the people invested in their lore and RP.

I have a dragon character that I’ve been thinking about recently, but I was wondering if it would be a good idea to go into an RP environment with a character like this in a vanilla setting (as I know there are people who RP as dragons in retail.)
The character is a dragon taking the form of a Tauren, going by the name of ‘Enya’adriel’. Posing as merely a wandering minstrel, and a healer of sorts, the Tauren keeps an eye on the flow of time throughout his travels, making sure there are no disturbances. His true name is Enyadormu, he’s a member of the Bronze dragonflight.
Whether I would ever reveal this to people in-character is questionable, and I’m not sure whether him being a dragon is lore-abiding, or even necessary. I’d love it to be a interesting feature for the character though?

What are your thoughts? Given that at some point, the devs want to open up the Caverns of Time and use it for something at some point, would this character be alright?

author: Parcival
subject: Re: Would it be alright to Roleplay as a Dragon?
content_md:
Roleplaying as a Dragon is tricky business - pretty much any role which in itself contains tremendous power is tricky business. There's a fine line here between being powerful and power-emoting. In casual RP occasions, it shouldn't be a problem, but it can quickly escalate into one, whenever you're in a fight.

I've seen my share of bad power hungry RP'ers; from demigod warlocks to dragons, and let me just say, none of those encounters was in any way rewarding or fun. There's just something foul, when someone begins with such power without having earned it. But hey, maybe you'll be different. So try it, why not - just be careful.

 *The cold wind carries with it, a most terrifying message of great danger ahead, waiting patiently in your near future. Omens of misfortune follow you, while your shadow dissipates with each passing day. In what wretchedness one must wallow, with no end at sight. Yet yours is not a tale of sorrow, at least - not yet. author: Parcival
subject: The Prima Scriptura - Paladin RP Guide
content_md:
> Disclaimer: All rights and credit for the guide goes to Anne Stickney. The original topic can be reached here: [https://www.engadget.com/2012-11-17-for ... ccounter=1](https://www.engadget.com/2012-11-17-for-the-light-roleplaying-the-paladin.html?guccounter=1)

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/ypZNbKr.png)

The paladin is a warrior of the Holy Light -- a person of exceedingly strong moral convictions who fights just as valiantly as any warrior on the field. However, it's his morals and his faith that make him differ from the usual warrior you see on the battlefield. Paladins are known to uphold all that is good in the world, fighting against all that is evil.

> In all things, a paladin must reflect the Light which supplements our strength. To strive to be divine for one of our kind does not mean we strive for godhood--we strive to be good in all actions.

The paladin is a follower of the Holy Light. This isn't necessarily a theistic belief system so much as a philosophy that is carefully practiced by both priests and paladins of the Order. The Holy Light is almost a "pay it forward" system of charitable deeds and actions, one that works on the presumption that there is an innate connection between self and the rest of the universe. Emotion connects an individual to the universe -- and being true to one's own emotions will cause emotion in others, creating a ripple effect of good in the universe.

> Valor, and all the virtues that go along with it, are like rare minerals: you must cherish them when you find them because of their value, but you must also take time to harvest them... refine them. When mixed together properly, a strong alloy is formed, sometimes unbreakable by even the most powerful blows.
>
>  This strength, your faith, your bravery, must be tested. You must learn to never lose faith and realize that with the power of the Light, you can overcome things that most others cannot.

When the tenets of the Holy Light are practiced to full extent, a paladin can never truly die -- his deeds, actions, and words will live on in perpetuity, continuing to inspire others for ages to come.

The origins and purpose of paladins, are something that the paladin has likely been taught ever since he decided to become a paladin. Being a paladin ties into exactly who he is at his core. There is no such thing as an "evil paladin" -- because a paladin that seeks to spread evil in the world will soon find himself with absolutely no access to the Light at all. It will abandon him.

> Bravery, regardless of the situation, is as much a part of paladinhood as the Light, your armor, and your weapon. Protecting the weak, and not losing faith are two more lessons you must master while you study in the Cathedral of Light.

The paladin is in a constant struggle with what the world is, and who they are being in the face of it. A paladin can absolutely be upset, despairing, or even angry at the world -- but his status as a paladin shifts with his moral convictions. One wrong decision won't ruin a paladin, but it will weigh on his mind far more heavily than your average adventurer. And while there may not be evil paladins in the world, there are those that are zealous to the point of seeming madness. The paladins of the Scarlet Crusade are a good example. They practice the Light, and the Light grants them power, even though they use that power for what seems to be evil intent to an outside observer. But to a member of the Scarlet Crusade, their devotion is and has always been to the Light. Their conviction is to eradicate the undead -- it's simply that they view anyone that is not a member of their organization as a potential undead waiting to happen.

> Although called upon to smite evil in these harsh times, you must always remember that it's aiding others that will truly set you apart from the citizens of Azeroth. Compassion, patience, bravery--these things mean as much to a paladin as strength in battle.

It's that conviction behind them that keeps the Light on their side, because that conviction is for the purpose of good. So one could easily roleplay a religious zealot of a paladin -- one who is convinced that his reasonings are the right reasonings, regardless of whether or not the rest of the world views it that way.

author: Drajj
subject: From Sand to Ash
content_md:
Greetings Turtle Wow community! I recently came across a post by both Lantsei & Jam(Rekgor) about a Hardcore Nomadic Challenge. Personally I love the idea and think its a great way to spice up my playthrough. The rules I'll be following are similar to Lantsei with only a minor change:
- Using Turtle WoWs Hardcore Mode (before level 10)

- No Dungeons | Battlegrounds | Raids

- You’re only able to use gear you yourself have crafted, earned from questing, looted, or bought from the AH

- Auction house can be used to sell materials

- All buffs must be self-applied e.g scrolls

- All secondary Professions are allowed, including the Survival Skill

- No aid from other players (buffs, gear, etc.)

- You are given two lives, if you die twice, it is all over; may your soul walk the Halls of Valor

- Reaching level 60 will allow you to keep your character even if they die. For having avoided death so long, they are now able to escape its permanence and return to the living!
The reason I include purchases from Quests and the Auction House is because I'm playing a Sand Troll that only uses rough or tribal looking armor/weapons. Other than making quests to facilitate such a requirement (which I might do reasonably), I figure why not give others a chance to make some coin by buying up any "rustic" looking items on the AH. So if you find anything for a desert dwelling rogue, get in touch or wait for me to buy it!

Now I'm currently lv 20 but luckily I'm already doing Hardcore Mode and have only died once to a minion of Agamand, so I'm only down to 1 life left! Whenever on I'm IC so feel free to exchange stories or say hello.

Periodically I'll update this post on progress, custom quest/npc details, or if Drajj has passed on from sand to ash...

 *"Our bodies be blistered and cracked wit da hardship of Tanaris. Dis pain be nut'in new to a Dunefury.*" -Drajj
